We appreciate your contributions to the ApexHip engineering team and look forward to supporting your continued development with Advanced Materials R&D.

Sincerely,

PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL

The Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation has entered its transfer order consolidating the pending ApexHip cases as MDL No. 3102 in the Northern District of Indiana. We expect additional filings promptly now that a centralized forum is in place.

The allegations are not uniform in every respect, but the core clinical narrative is becoming notably consistent: elevated cobalt/chromium levels, ARMD-type findings, early revision, and an assertion that Veridian had sufficient registry and complaint information to alter the product’s market status earlier than it did. A number of complaints specifically track the themes raised in our internal 2021 registry work.

Dana and Leon, please reassess whether the registry-based rationale supporting continued market availability after the September 2021 Signal Review remains supportable in light of the volume and consistency of allegations now being made. I am not asking for a litigation assessment or a rewrite of historical materials. I need the regulatory and clinical view, based on the information available then and now, including the NJR and AJRR data, the labeling update, the October 2021 surgeon communication, and subsequent surveillance.

Owen, please have your team identify any financial or operational assumptions that depended on continued Apex availability through 2024. Rob, we will provide a separate overview of likely timing and governance needs once the MDL leadership structure is established.

I am setting a joint call for next week with Dana, Leon, Greg Novak, and Priya Raman. Please come prepared to discuss the record, not messaging. Do not forward this email.

Rachel

From: Dr. Anita Rao <arao@nashvillehipknee.com>
To: Priya Raman <praman@veridianortho.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2021 16:42
Subject: Revision case - cobalt levels and pseudotumor

Priya,

I wanted to make you aware of a revision I performed this week on an ApexHip patient implanted in 2018. The cup was lot V-2091. She presented with increasing groin pain and a sense of instability. Her cobalt and chromium levels were both elevated, and the MARS MRI showed a fluid collection/pseudotumor with tissue changes that, clinically, are consistent with an adverse reaction to metal debris.

We revised the construct and sent the tissue and components for the usual workup. My operative impression was not simply a loose or infected hip; there was substantial dark staining and reactive tissue around the joint.

I am becoming concerned this is not an isolated event among my Apex patients. I have had several patients with symptoms or ion results that merit closer follow-up, although not all have required revision.

I recently read the March NJR report and noted the revision-rate signal for Apex compared with the class average. Has Veridian compiled aggregate data on cobalt/chromium elevations, ARMD findings, or revisions across sites? And have you seen anything similar in the registry data beyond what is publicly reported?

Please let me know who should receive the case details and explant information. I would appreciate a candid answer on the broader experience.

Best,

Anita Rao, MD
Nashville Hip & Knee

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS QUALITY ASSURANCE
RECALL EFFECTIVENESS SUMMARY REPORT

Reference: RES-2022-04 (FDA Recall Event Z-1418-2022)
Product: ApexHip Acetabular Cup (Lots V-2200 through V-2299)
Period: 30-Day Milestone Review
Date Generated: July 18, 2022
Prepared By: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

Executive Overview

Per Veridian SOP-QA-408 and 21 CFR 7.42, a 30-day effectiveness evaluation was conducted for the voluntary Class II recall of ApexHip acetabular cups associated with plasma-spray coating non-conformances. Initial customer notifications and consignee acknowledgment forms were dispatched commencing June 14, 2022.

Overall, 210 direct consignee accounts were identified and contacted across domestic sales territories. To date, 189 accounts have returned signed verification forms, establishing a 90.0% initial response rate. Among responding facilities, 6 affected units have been located and physically quarantined pending return authorization (RGA), and 2 units were confirmed implanted prior to notification receipt (both cases monitored; no adverse events reported). Field follow-ups remain active for the 21 pending consignees.

Regional Breakdown

| Region | Accounts Contacted | Responses Received | Response Rate (%) | Units Quarantined | Units Implanted | Pending Accounts |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Southeast (Atlanta Hub) | 82 | 78 | 95.1% | 3 | 1 | 4 |
| Midwest (Warsaw/Chicago) | 64 | 60 | 93.8% | 2 | 0 | 4 |
| West (Denver/Dallas) | 64 | 51 | 79.7% | 1 | 1 | 13 |
| Total | 210 | 189 | 90.0% | 6 | 2 | 21 |

Corrective Follow-Up

The West region currently exhibits the highest pending count (13 accounts), primarily concentrated among municipal facilities and Northgate-adjacent regional surgical centers in the Denver district. Second-notice certified mailings and local sales rep escalations have been initiated per TrackWise record TW-2022-0614. Next effectiveness audit scheduled at the 60-day mark (August 15, 2022).

PRESENTATION NOTES

Veridian Orthopedics — Reconstructive Sales
Q1 2022 Objection Handling Refresh: Recall Context
Prepared by: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
Date: January 11, 2022
Distribution: Reconstructive sales team (internal use only — do not forward externally)

Purpose
As we prep the field for potential questions ahead of any customer-facing communications on the cup lot matter, I want to make sure everyone is drawing a clean line between two separate topics. We've seen some blending of these in call notes and I want to nip that before it becomes a pattern.

Two distinct issues — keep them separate

1. Coating/lot issue (Cork manufacturing) — a limited number of acetabular cup lots (V-2200 through V-2299, produced Nov 2021–Feb 2022) showed a coating adhesion irregularity identified during incoming inspection at two facilities. This is a manufacturing quality matter tied to a specific production window. Quality and Regulatory are running lot traceability now; more to follow from Dana's team on timing/scope.

2. Bearing surface / revision rate discussion — this is the ongoing, industry-wide conversation around metal-on-metal wear performance and registry data (NJR, AJRR) that surgeons have been raising since last fall. That's a separate clinical topic and is already addressed in the FAQ Priya's and Dana's teams sent out in September, along with the Dear Doctor letter and label update language.

Suggested script if asked
"This is a manufacturing quality issue with a specific batch, separate from the industry-wide bearing surface discussion. We identified it through our own inspection process and are addressing it directly with affected accounts. It's not related to the wear performance questions you may have seen in the registry data — that's a separate topic we've already given you materials on."

Do
- Refer back to the September FAQ for revision-rate/registry questions.
- Keep coating questions focused on lot numbers, not wear mechanism.
- Loop in your RSM if a surgeon pushes on both topics at once.

Don't
- Speculate on root cause beyond "manufacturing process deviation under review."
- Use the words "recall" or "withdrawal" until we have official notice language — more on that soon.

Questions to me or Jenna. Thanks for staying disciplined on this — it matters.

meta.gray_rationale: Discusses the recall by name and lot numbers as part of scripting guidance, which a reviewer could view as recall-related content even though the arc's focus is sales messaging.

From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
To: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Cc: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
Subject: Re-test results at 55 degree inclination - concerning wear rates

Priya, Carlos,

I'm writing this up formally because I don't think an email does it justice. As some of you know I've been unhappy with the DR-3 wear-test protocol for a while now — we only ran ISO 14242 at the standard 45 degree cup inclination, which is fine per the standard but doesn't reflect what I'm seeing in surgeon feedback about cup placement in the field. So I asked Meridian to re-run a set of samples at 55 degrees to see what happens.

The results are bad. Attached is Apex_wear_55deg_rev2.xlsx — columns are inclination angle, wear volume (mm3/million cycles), and head diameter. At 45 degrees we're seeing our expected baseline, roughly 0.8-1.2 mm3/Mc depending on head size (36-44mm range tested). At 55 degrees the same lots are producing 4-6x that volume, in the 4.5-6.8 mm3/Mc range. This is edge loading — the head is contacting the rim of the cup instead of the deep articulating surface, and at that inclination the wear mechanism basically changes character. It's not a small effect and it's not noise, I re-ran three sample sets and got the same pattern each time.

The uncomfortable question is how many of our implanted cups are sitting at 50+ degrees of inclination in actual patients. I don't have great visibility into that — that's more Priya's world with complaint data and maybe something Novak could pull from registry angle data if it's even captured — but anecdotally I know cup positioning varies a lot surgeon to surgeon, and nobody is checking inclination angle at 45 degrees with a protractor in the OR. If even a meaningful minority of our patients are outside the tested envelope, we have a real gap between what we validated and what's happening clinically.

I think we need to look seriously at the cup rim geometry. A few options I'd want on the table: increasing rim coverage/height to reduce edge contact at higher inclinations, revisiting the head-to-cup clearance, or possibly a chamfer redesign. None of these are trivial changes to a cleared device but I don't think we can just sit on this data.

I'd like to convene a design review — not a full DR, but something focused — to walk through this and talk about whether we open an ECO. I can have a full test report finished within two weeks but wanted you both to see the raw numbers now rather than wait.

Let me know your thinking. I'd rather over-communicate this than have it sit in my inbox.

Tom

MEMORANDUM

TO: Dana Okonkwo (VP, Regulatory Affairs), Rachel Steinberg (General Counsel), Dr. Leon Adeyemi (Chief Medical Officer), Marcus Lee (VP, Sales)
FROM: Carlos Mendes (Product Manager, ApexHip)
DATE: September 28, 2021
SUBJECT: Draft "Dear Doctor" Letter – ApexHip Acetabular System Labeling Update

Following the decisions reached during our September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, I have prepared the initial draft text for the upcoming customer notification ("Dear Doctor" letter) regarding the ApexHip Total Hip System.

As agreed by the review team and executive leadership, Veridian will maintain active commercial distribution of ApexHip while implementing an immediate Instructions for Use (IFU) labeling update to address emerging registry trends.

Background & Signal Summary
The primary driver for this communication is data presented from the March 2021 National Joint Registry (NJR) 17th Annual Report, which identified a cumulative 5-year revision rate of 7.1% for the ApexHip construct, compared to an average class benchmark of approximately 3.2% across contemporary metal-on-metal (MoM) hip resurfacing and total replacement systems. While internal clinical evaluations indicate that well-positioned constructs continue to demonstrate strong clinical survivorship, registry data and internal engineering assessments correlate early revisions predominantly with adverse local tissue reactions (ALTR/ARMD) linked to elevated cobalt and chromium ion levels.

Proposed Letter Content & Labeling Guidance
The draft notification emphasizes patient safety, precise surgical technique, and targeted post-operative vigilance:

1. Patient Monitoring Recommendations: We advise clinicians to establish heightened routine clinical and radiographic follow-up protocols for all implanted ApexHip patients, with particular attention to individuals receiving larger femoral head diameters (≥44 mm). Routine cross-sectional imaging (MARS-MRI or ultrasound) and periodic blood metal-ion quantification (whole blood cobalt and chromium) should be considered annually or upon any presentation of unexplained pain, clicking, or swelling.
2. Surgical Positioning & Angle Inclination: Revisions strongly correlate with edge-loading phenomena. The revised labeling explicitly instructs surgeons to target an acetabular cup inclination angle within 40° to 45° and anteversion between 15° and 20°. Operating outside these ranges—specifically exceeding 50° of operative abduction—markedly increases the risk of accelerated fluid-film wear and premature component loosening.

Next Steps & Timeline
Our target mail date to all US and EU implanting orthopedic surgeons, chief medical officers, and relevant risk management personnel is mid-October 2021. Reps will receive accompanying talking points once this text is locked.

Please review the attached formal notification layout (`Apex_Dear_Doctor_Draft_v1.docx`) and provide your redlines. We require formal sign-off from Regulatory Affairs, Legal, and Clinical before Dana submits the final package to the agency and we proceed with mass distribution.

From: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer

Subject: Annual review of KOL compensation spend - Apex program

I have completed Finance’s annual review of the ApexHip key opinion leader and physician-engagement spend through September 30, including the supporting invoices, speaker-program records, travel and expense submissions, and royalty reporting provided by Commercial Operations.

At a program level, the spend remains within the board-approved physician consulting and education budget. Apex continues to be a meaningful growth driver, and the clinical education component remains important to adoption, particularly for surgeons new to the larger-head MoM procedure. That said, the concentration of spend among a small number of physicians is worth continued attention, both from a budget-management standpoint and in light of increasing regulatory scrutiny of device-maker relationships with KOLs industry-wide.

The figures below exclude ordinary customer meals below the company reporting threshold, product evaluation units, and broader professional-society sponsorships. They include amounts processed through Accounts Payable and Concur as of September 30. Q4 estimates are not included.

| Physician / group | Payment category | 2019 Q1–Q4 | 2020 Q1–Q3 | 2019–2020 YTD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Dr. Marcus Feld | Consulting/design advisory | $82,500 | $61,250 | $143,750 |
| Dr. Marcus Feld | Royalty payments | $32,400 | $20,100 | $52,500 |
| Dr. Marcus Feld | Travel, lodging and meeting expenses | $5,900 | $2,850 | $8,750 |
| Dr. Marcus Feld subtotal |  | $120,800 | $84,200 | $205,000 |
| Dr. Anita Rao | Speaker honoraria | $28,500 | $21,000 | $49,500 |
| Dr. Anita Rao | Travel, lodging and meeting expenses | $4,100 | $4,400 | $8,500 |
| Dr. Anita Rao subtotal |  | $32,600 | $25,400 | $58,000 |
| Four regional surgeons | Case observations / proctoring support | $12,000 | $10,000 | $22,000 |
| Total Apex KOL and physician-engagement spend |  | $165,400 | $119,600 | $285,000 |

The four regional-surgeon arrangements are individually modest and relate primarily to case observation, peer-to-peer education, and feedback following early use of Apex at sites where we were building a reference base. The participating surgeons were Dr. Paul Neri (Dallas), Dr. Allison Kane (Charlotte), Dr. Miguel Santos (Orlando), and Dr. Ethan Brooks (Denver). Payment files generally identify the applicable program and dates of service. A few older files rely on Sales’ event records rather than a standalone engagement summary; those should be cleaned up before any renewal or new work is approved.

Dr. Feld remains the largest individual recipient because he has three distinct relationships with Veridian: design consulting, speaker-program participation, and the royalty arrangement associated with his Apex design contribution. The royalty calculation was reconciled to the underlying agreement and quarterly sales data. Finance did not identify a payment outside the agreement terms. Nevertheless, the cumulative number will attract attention simply because of its size and his visibility in the Apex program. Marcus, please make sure field personnel understand that consulting status does not change the approval process for customer-related expenses, product requests, or speaking engagements.

Dr. Rao’s spend is principally honoraria for approved educational programs, with limited travel associated with advisory-board and faculty activity. Her total is consistent with prior periods and below the annual planning assumption. I note that several 2020 programs moved to virtual delivery, which accounts for the lower travel component but does not eliminate the need for attendance records, agenda support, and documented educational content.

My recommendation is not to reduce the program solely because it is concentrated. Rather, we should tighten the file discipline around fair-market-value determinations and business justification. Specifically:

1. Commercial should retain a current FMV analysis for each consulting, faculty, advisory-board, and case-observation rate, rather than relying on a prior-year rate card without an explicit renewal review.

2. Each engagement should have a short statement of need tied to a defined service: design input, training, case observation, or an approved educational presentation. “Relationship development” is not an adequate description for the file.

3. Travel should be supported by a program agenda and actual attendance or service confirmation. Finance will continue to reject unsupported upgrades, companion travel, and expenses without a clear business purpose.

4. Royalty administration should remain segregated from speaker and consulting approvals. The contracts are different, and the record should make that distinction obvious.

5. Legal and Compliance should confirm that the current Sunshine reporting mapping captures all payment types consistently, including travel booked centrally and expenses reimbursed through Concur.

Rachel, I would appreciate Legal’s view on whether the current consulting-agreement templates and FMV memoranda need updating before the 2021 renewals. Marcus, Commercial Operations should identify the engagement owner for every active Apex physician file by October 30. Finance can provide the underlying transaction listing if helpful, but I would prefer we resolve missing support prospectively rather than reconstruct it at year-end.

The program is within budget and has not created a forecast issue. The more relevant concern is that our records should demonstrate that we are paying for legitimate, defined services at supportable rates, particularly as the industry receives more attention in this area.

Owen

She flagged this is consistent with what Tom's 2019 55-degree wear-test re-analysis predicted.

2. ECO-2019-118 Status (Halvorsen)

Tom confirmed the design change proposal (cup geometry / edge-loading mitigation) remains deferred per the 2019 design review decision. No new engineering work has been authorized since. Tom asked whether the updated complaint numbers change the calculus on revisiting it.

3. Discussion

Dana asked whether the complaint increase alone would trigger a design review reopening under our procedures; Priya said not automatically, but sustained upward trend plus registry data (NJR report expected later this year) could support it.

Carlos noted that 2020 is tracking to be Apex's best sales year yet — Q1 bookings are strong and the sales team is counting on continued momentum. He cautioned that any visible design-change activity, even internal, carries risk of leaking into the field and being read by surgeons or competitors as an admission of a problem, at a commercially sensitive moment. He was not opposed to engineering work continuing quietly but urged against any external-facing announcement or labeling change right now.

No consensus reached on reopening ECO-2019-118. Group agreed the complaint trend is worth continued close monitoring.

4. Action Items

- Raman to pull complete Q2 complaint data and re-run the trend comparison by mid-July.
- Halvorsen to keep wear-test analysis materials current in case design review is reopened.

Dana, Greg,

Wanted to put some additional thoughts down after Tuesday's meeting, mostly for my own clarity but also so we're aligned going forward.

The 7.1% five-year revision rate in the NJR report is genuinely concerning to me as a clinician, and I don't want that to get lost in how we're framing this internally. That said, I think we need to hold two possibilities open at once. The literature on edge-loading at high inclination angles is fairly consistent with what Tom's 2019 wear-test work showed at 55 degrees — and that pattern is often surgical-technique dependent rather than a pure implant design failure. Cup positioning variability across surgeons could be doing real work here, and that's not something a labeling change alone fixes, but it does mean I'm not ready to call this a design defect on the current data.

Given that, I support moving quickly on the labeling update — the sooner surgeons are reminded about inclination targets, the better. I'd also like us to pull PMS data again in six months rather than waiting for the next annual cycle.

I'm comfortable with continuing to sell under these conditions for now. But if the AJRR Q1 2022 numbers move in the wrong direction, I think we need to revisit this decision seriously.

Leon

MEETING MINUTES

Registry Signal Review Meeting
Date: September 14, 2021
Time: 9:00–10:00 AM
Location: The Hub — Reserve B
Prepared by: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs

Attendees: Dana Okonkwo; Greg Novak; Priya Raman; Dr. Leon Adeyemi; Carlos Mendes; Marcus Lee; Rachel Steinberg
By phone: Rob Castellano, CEO

Purpose
To review the current ApexHip registry signal and determine whether continued commercialization with additional risk mitigation remains appropriate.

Discussion

1. Registry data. Greg Novak presented the March 2021 NJR annual-report data. ApexHip’s reported five-year revision rate is 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average. The difference remains after available review of age and head-size strata, although the registry does not permit a complete adjustment for surgeon technique, patient selection, or cup position.

Greg also reviewed the most recent AJRR extracts. The AJRR population is less mature than the NJR cohort, but the direction is consistent: an upward trend in early revisions, including records identifying elevated metal ions, ARMD, unexplained pain, and loosening among reported indications. Greg noted limitations in indication coding and data completeness. He recommended monthly monitoring until the next formal registry refresh.

2. Clinical interpretation. Dr. Adeyemi stated that the signal is concerning and warrants active mitigation. He did not believe the currently available registry information alone establishes a design defect or supports an immediate conclusion that all ApexHip recipients face the same level of risk. He noted that cup inclination, patient activity, and other clinical variables may be relevant to metal-on-metal wear and revision risk. His recommendation was closer monitoring, clearer surgeon guidance on patient selection and surgical technique, and prompt review of new clinical information rather than immediate market withdrawal.

3. Regulatory and complaint considerations. Dana Okonkwo reviewed the need to continue evaluating reportability and trend information under 21 CFR 803. Priya Raman confirmed that complaints involving elevated cobalt/chromium levels, ARMD, pseudotumor findings, unexplained pain, and revisions are being entered and assessed in TrackWise per procedure. Dana emphasized that complaint trending, MDR decisions, and registry surveillance must remain aligned and contemporaneously documented.

4. Commercial and communications considerations. Carlos Mendes and Marcus Lee discussed the operational impact of a withdrawal versus revised labeling and field communication. Marcus noted the need for clear, controlled guidance for the sales organization if ApexHip remains available. Rachel Steinberg requested that external communications accurately describe the available data and not characterize the registry findings as conclusive.

Decision

The group agreed to continue selling ApexHip at this time, subject to the following risk-mitigation measures:

• Implement a labeling update emphasizing appropriate surgical technique, including cup inclination angle, patient selection, and clinical follow-up considerations.
• Prepare a Dear Doctor letter for distribution to implanting surgeons in October 2021.
• Increase post-market complaint and registry trend monitoring.

Rob Castellano joined by phone for the decision discussion and concurred with the above approach.

Action Items

1. Carlos Mendes: Coordinate proposed ApexHip labeling revisions with Regulatory, Clinical, and Marketing. Initial draft due September 24.
2. Devon Mitchell: Prepare Dear Doctor letter draft for Regulatory and Legal review. Initial draft due September 27.
3. Priya Raman: Establish enhanced complaint-trend monitoring and provide a monthly summary to Regulatory and PMS beginning October 2021.
4. Greg Novak: Continue monthly NJR/AJRR surveillance and escalate material changes promptly.
5. Dana Okonkwo: Confirm regulatory documentation and review requirements for the labeling update and surgeon communication.

Dana

Re: MDL No. 3102 — Case Management Update and Fee Estimate

Dear Rachel:

I write with a brief status update following the Court’s initial case-management conference in MDL No. 3102.

The plaintiffs’ steering committee has now been appointed. We expect plaintiffs’ leadership to move quickly on master pleadings, a consolidated fact sheet, and initial discovery proposals. The Court has indicated that it wants an orderly but active schedule and has identified bellwether selection as a Q3 2024 objective. That timing is aspirational at this stage, but it is consistent with the Court’s comments that the parties should begin developing a usable pool of representative cases rather than litigating every threshold issue serially.

As of this week, we are tracking approximately 340 filed or transferred cases, with new matters arriving weekly. The present inventory is sufficiently large that we should plan for substantial common-discovery activity even if the bellwether schedule moves. We are continuing to evaluate the allegations by implant configuration, treating surgeon, revision timing, and claimed injury, particularly with respect to cobalt/chromium levels and ARMD allegations.

For budgeting purposes, our updated estimate for 2024 defense costs is $6 million to $9 million. This range includes lead counsel work, common discovery, expert consultation and development, document collection and review support, and anticipated motion practice through year-end. It does not include any settlement funding, reserve adjustment, or unusual trial-preparation expenditures should the Court accelerate the bellwether track.

We also recommend that Veridian begin considering whether to explore mediation later this year. This is not a recommendation to make an immediate offer. However, given the volume and trajectory of filings, early evaluation of a mediation structure may provide useful optionality once the parties have exchanged sufficient case-specific information.

Finally, plaintiffs’ counsel continue to reference the 2022 coating recall, FDA Recall No. Z-1418-2022. As we have discussed, that recall concerned KinetiCoat adhesion in specified cup lots and is distinct from the metal-ion and wear allegations driving the MDL. Plaintiffs nevertheless appear likely to use the recall rhetorically to suggest a broader product-quality narrative. We will continue to keep those issues clearly separated in pleadings, discovery, and expert work.

Please do not forward. I am available to discuss the estimate and mediation timing at your convenience.

Sales Training Call — Speaker Notes

Date: September 27, 2021
Prepared by: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
Subject: Answering the Metal Ion Question — Training Notes

These notes support the September 30 field call. Please use the approved language as written where possible. The objective is to be responsive and credible without making clinical interpretations in the field.

Slide 1 — Opening

“Surgeons are seeing more questions around cobalt and chromium testing generally, including from patients who have read about metal-on-metal hips. Our role is to acknowledge the question, explain the information available in the product labeling, and connect the physician with the appropriate Veridian clinical resource when interpretation is needed.”

Do not characterize a patient’s result as normal, abnormal, concerning, or unrelated to the implant. Do not compare one patient’s value to another patient’s value.

Slide 2 — If asked: “Do ApexHip patients have elevated ions?”

Suggested response:

“Cobalt and chromium ion monitoring is an established topic across metal-on-metal hip systems and should be considered by the treating physician in the context of the individual patient. ApexHip labeling addresses follow-up and clinical evaluation considerations. We are in the process of implementing an updated label to provide additional clarity for surgeons.”

Avoid: “Apex does not cause elevated ions,” “the levels are harmless,” or “this is expected.”

If a surgeon asks whether ApexHip is the cause of a particular lab result, say:

“I can’t interpret an individual laboratory value or determine causation. I can connect you with Medical Affairs so the appropriate clinical discussion can occur.”

Route all lab-value, imaging, revision, pseudotumor, tissue-reaction, or causation questions to Medical Affairs. Do not collect or summarize clinical details by text message. Follow the complaint intake procedure if the surgeon is reporting a potential product complaint.

Slide 3 — Registry question / March 2021 NJR data

The March 2021 NJR annual report includes a five-year ApexHip revision rate of 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average. Do not dispute the figure, speculate about registry methodology, or provide your own explanation for the difference.

Approved framing:

“The published registry figures should be viewed in the context of broader industry variance, including patient selection, surgeon practice, follow-up patterns, and differences in reporting populations. Regulatory has reviewed the language we are using, and the updated labeling will provide additional information for clinicians.”

If pressed, repeat the published figures accurately and offer to arrange a discussion with Medical Affairs or Post-Market Surveillance. Do not say that the rate is “within normal range” or that it is “not statistically meaningful.”

Slide 4 — Label update

“The label update is in progress. It is intended to give surgeons clearer follow-up information and does not change the need for physicians to exercise their independent clinical judgment.”

Do not provide an expected approval or release date. Do not distribute draft label language.

Slide 5 — Keeping product messaging distinct

KneeFlex may be used as a simple example of product-specific messaging: “KneeFlex is a different platform and does not involve the same metal-on-metal bearing discussion.” Do not broaden that statement into a comparative safety claim or suggest that no KneeFlex issues have ever been reported.

Close with: “Be calm, be factual, and escalate clinical interpretation. We earn trust by not overreaching.”

SUBJECT: Voluntary Permanent Market Withdrawal – ApexHip Total Hip System (510(k) K162447)

Dear CDRH Office of Compliance:

This letter serves as formal notification that Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. ("Veridian") has initiated a voluntary permanent market withdrawal of the ApexHip Total Hip System, originally cleared under 510(k) K162447 on March 9, 2017. Effective February 2, 2024, Veridian has ceased all commercial distribution and sales of all components of the ApexHip system across all domestic and international markets.

Veridian has structured and initiated the following actions pursuant to 21 CFR Part 806:

1. Scope and Distinction from Prior Regulatory Actions: This voluntary withdrawal encompasses all sizes and lots of the ApexHip acetabular cups (sizes 44–62 mm), femoral heads (sizes 36–50 mm), and associated femoral stems. Please note that this comprehensive commercial withdrawal is separate and distinct from the prior voluntary Class II recall initiated on June 14, 2022 (Recall Number Z-1418-2022), which was strictly confined to cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 concerning KinetiCoat plasma-spray adhesion anomalies.

2. Underlying Basis for Withdrawal: Ongoing evaluation of cumulative post-market surveillance data, specifically longitudinal data sets published in external joint registries including the UK National Joint Registry (NJR) and the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR), indicates an elevated long-term cumulative revision rate associated with metal-on-metal articulation that exceeds acceptable comparative class performance thresholds. While previous labeling updates and clinical communications sought to address surgical technique and patient selection parameters, Veridian has determined that permanent cessation of sales is the appropriate risk-mitigation measure.

3. Field Correction and Inventory Quarantine: All regional sales offices, contract distributors, and hospital consignments have been formally instructed to cease implantation immediately. Field representatives have initiated the physical recovery and return of all non-implanted inventory to our central distribution facility in Warsaw, Indiana, where products will be placed under strict QA quarantine pending destruction.

4. Surgeon and Facility Notification: Direct written communication to all operating surgeons, risk management departments, and hospital purchasing administrators is underway, providing monitoring guidance and clinical follow-up recommendations for existing implanted patients.

Veridian will provide the CDRH Office of Compliance with bi-weekly progress reports detailing inventory reconciliation and customer notification confirmation until final closeout.

Respectfully submitted,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

1180 Research Park Drive, Indianapolis, Indiana 46202

14 August 2019

To: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.
4400 Silver Lake Blvd
Warsaw, Indiana 46580

Subject: ISO 14242 Wear Test Report – ApexHip Supplemental Inclination Study

Dear Mr. Halvorsen:

At Veridian Orthopedics’ request, Meridian Testing Labs conducted a supplemental simulator wear study of the ApexHip metal-on-metal total hip bearing under elevated acetabular cup inclination. This work was requested as an extension of the previously completed ISO 14242 protocol testing conducted at the standard 45-degree cup orientation.

Study Objective
The objective was to compare volumetric wear, visual bearing surface condition, and cobalt/chromium release rates for ApexHip constructs tested at 55 degrees inclination against the established 45-degree control configuration.

Test Articles
Six ApexHip bearing constructs were evaluated. Test articles consisted of Co/Cr acetabular cups from the V-2100 series and matching Co/Cr femoral heads from the H-3050 series. The cup lots included V-2108, V-2113, and V-2121; head lots included H-3052, H-3057, and H-3061. Components were supplied by Veridian and inspected upon receipt for packaging integrity and visible defects. No pre-test anomalies were observed.

Methodology
Testing was performed using six-station hip joint simulators in accordance with ISO 14242 loading and motion profiles, except for the specified acetabular orientation. Three stations were configured at 45 degrees inclination and served as controls. Three stations were configured at 55 degrees inclination. All stations were operated for 5 million cycles at 1 Hz under bovine serum lubricant diluted to 25 g/L total protein concentration. Lubricant was changed at 0.5 million-cycle intervals.

Gravimetric measurements were taken at each lubricant interval after cleaning and drying pursuant to laboratory procedure MTL-WEAR-014. Lubricant samples were retained at each interval and analyzed by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry for cobalt and chromium content. Bearing surfaces were examined by optical microscopy at completion.

Results
The 45-degree control group demonstrated cumulative volumetric wear consistent with prior ApexHip simulator work. The 55-degree group showed a material increase beginning between 1.0 and 1.5 million cycles, with the differential increasing through the end of the study.

| Configuration | Mean Cumulative Wear at 5M Cycles | Mean Co/Cr Release Rate |
|---|---:|---:|
| 45-degree inclination | 14.2 mm³ | 0.18 mg/million cycles |
| 55-degree inclination | 71.6 mm³ | 0.94 mg/million cycles |

The elevated-inclination group therefore exhibited approximately five times the volumetric wear and metal ion release rate observed in the 45-degree control group. Two of three 55-degree stations also demonstrated localized polishing and stripe wear near the superior rim of the cup, consistent with edge-loading contact. These features were not observed to the same extent in the control group.

Conclusion
Under the conditions tested, elevated cup inclination materially increased wear of the ApexHip metal-on-metal bearing. Clinical cup positioning above approximately 50 degrees inclination presents an elevated risk of edge loading, increased wear volume, and increased cobalt/chromium release relative to the standard 45-degree orientation.

This report is provided to Mr. Halvorsen for internal distribution to the Veridian design team. It should be considered together with the applicable design inputs, risk analysis, and clinical evaluation materials.

Sincerely,

Meridian Testing Labs

Elaine Porter, Ph.D.
Director, Biomechanical Evaluation Services

SUBJECT: Workforce Transition Plan - ApexHip Market Withdrawal

Following the February 2, 2024 announcement regarding the voluntary global market withdrawal of the ApexHip Total Hip System, Human Resources has finalized the workforce transition and organizational alignment plan.

While this market action impacts product line revenue and commercial focus, our regulatory, clinical, and quality obligations for previously implanted units remain fully active. Consequently, this plan balances necessary commercial consolidation with targeted personnel retention across technical operations.

1. Scope of Impacted Personnel

The withdrawal directly impacts positions dedicated exclusively to the commercialization, promotional positioning, and field support of ApexHip:

• Commercial Sales: Five (5) Regional Reconstruction Specialists whose sole portfolio assignment was ApexHip conversion accounts across the Southeast, Central, and Western territories. General reconstructive sales representatives carrying KneeFlex and shoulder lines will absorb remaining territory accounts and are unaffected by this reduction.
• Marketing Communications: Four (4) dedicated contractor roles within MarCom supporting Apex product campaigns, digital asset management, and agency liaison work (Kessler Reid deliverables). Contracts will be concluded effective February 29, 2024, per standard notice provisions.
• Operations / Field Inventory: Two (2) logistics coordinator roles in Warsaw supporting hospital consignment retrieval and field kit balancing.

2. Retention of Core Technical, Quality, and Regulatory Staff

It is critical to emphasize that no headcount reductions will occur within Product Development, Regulatory Affairs, Post-Market Surveillance, or Quality Complaint Handling.

Per 21 CFR 820 and 803 requirements, our post-market surveillance, adverse event trending, and complaint investigation responsibilities continue indefinitely for all legacy implanted ApexHip systems. The following teams will remain intact:

• Quality & Complaint Handling: Priya Raman’s team will maintain current staffing levels to manage incoming TrackWise complaint files, MDR determinations, and explant evaluations.
• Post-Market Surveillance: Greg Novak will continue overseeing registry monitoring (AJRR, NJR), signal detection, and ongoing surveillance reports.
• R&D Engineering: Lead sustaining engineer Wei Chen and supporting mechanical testing staff will remain fully allocated to ongoing retrieval analyses, wear simulator evaluations, and technical support for ongoing regulatory inquiries.

3. Severance and Transition Package Terms

For eligible regular full-time employees subject to position elimination, Veridian will offer standard severance packages structured as follows:

• Base Severance: Two (2) weeks of base pay per year of continuous service, with a minimum of eight (8) weeks and a maximum of twenty-six (26) weeks.
• Benefits Continuation: Employer-subsidized COBRA premium coverage corresponding to the severance duration period.
• Incentive Compensation: Pro-rated FY2024 target bonus payouts calculated through March 31, 2024.
• Outplacement Services: Three (3) months of executive and professional outplacement assistance via Lee Hecht Harrison (LHH).

4. Implementation Timeline

• Feb 5–Feb 9: Finalize Workday role status updates; prepare individualized separation documentation and release agreements with outside legal review.
• Feb 12–Feb 16: Manager briefing sessions; coordinate notification scheduling with VP Sales Marcus Lee and relevant regional directors.
• Feb 19–Feb 23: Conduct individual notification meetings with impacted commercial staff.
• Feb 29: Contract conclusion date for MarCom external contractors.
• March 29, 2024: Target final separation date for impacted regular employees.

Please direct any questions regarding specific employee conversations or Workday processing directly to me.

CC: Marcus Lee, VP Sales; Jenna Whitfield, Regional Sales Manager; Priya Raman, Director Quality & Complaint Handling; Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs
DATE: February 2, 2024
SUBJECT: Sales Guidance & Talking Points: ApexHip Voluntary Market Withdrawal

1. Administrative Overview & Logistics

Effective immediately, Friday, February 2, 2024, Veridian Orthopedics is initiating a voluntary commercial market withdrawal of the ApexHip Total Hip System (including all modular femoral heads, stems, and KinetiCoat acetabular cups).

All territory managers, sales representatives, and independent distributors must immediately pause any planned surgical implantations scheduled for Monday, February 5, onward. Coordination for return authorization numbers (RGA) and retrieval of hospital consignment and trunk inventory will commence next week via a structured inventory recovery portal managed through Agile PLM. Please ensure your accounts do not transfer stock between facilities.

While our primary immediate operational focus is inventory reconciliation and customer support, we recognize that surgeons, OR coordinators, and hospital risk managers will reach out to you with clinical and logistical inquiries throughout the day.

2. Clinical and Regulatory Context

To understand the environment prompting incoming surgeon contacts, reps should understand the context that has developed over recent reporting cycles. As communicated previously, international registry data—specifically the UK National Joint Registry (NJR) annual reporting which noted a cumulative 5-year revision rate of 7.1% for ApexHip (against an overall metal-on-metal benchmark of 3.2%)—alongside subsequent AJRR registry signals, led to our September 2021 Registry Signal Review and the October 2021 labeling update regarding patient positioning and cup inclination.

The decision announced today reflects leadership's ongoing evaluation of long-term commercial positioning in light of global MoM clinical registry trends and evolving reconstructive practice standards.

3. Approved Field Guidance: What to Say

When communicating with orthopaedic surgeons, surgical teams, and account administrators, stick strictly to the following approved messaging pillars:

*   Voluntary Action: "Veridian has elected to execute a proactive, voluntary market withdrawal of the ApexHip system from global distribution, effective February 2, 2024. This is a business and product line portfolio decision."
*   Asymptomatic Patients: "For patients currently implanted with ApexHip, the company is *not* recommending proactive surgical revision or prophylactic intervention in the absence of symptoms. Surgeons should continue standard postoperative follow-up protocols as outlined in the Instructions for Use (IFU)."
*   Symptomatic Inquiries & Medical Escalation: "If a patient presents with unresolved groin pain, swelling, or concerns regarding local tissue response, please advise the clinical team to evaluate per their standard clinical judgment. Do not offer medical advice or speculate on blood ion testing."
*   Dedicated Hotline Referral: Direct all technical, patient, or adverse-event inquiries directly to our dedicated Medical & Quality Information Hotline at extension 4880 (or via email at `clinicalsupport@veridianortho.com`), which is staffed and managed directly by Priya Raman’s Quality & Complaint Handling team. TrackWise intake numbers will be provided for any surgeon reporting an adverse event.

4. Critical Boundaries: What NOT to Say

To ensure alignment and prevent misinformation, field personnel are instructed to adhere strictly to the following restrictions:

*   Do NOT conflate this action with the 2022 coating recall. The June 2022 Class II recall (FDA Recall Z-1418-2022) involving Cork plasma-spray cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 was a distinct, isolated manufacturing adhesion issue that was fully remediated and closed. Do not discuss the coating recall in the same breath as this withdrawal; doing so creates profound clinical confusion regarding product wear vs. coating integrity.
*   Do NOT debate metal ion concentrations or registries. Never minimize NJR or AJRR data, but do not debate blood serum cobalt/chromium thresholds or adverse local tissue reaction (ALTR/ARMD) mechanisms with clinicians.
*   Do NOT comment on legal matters. If asked about ongoing product liability litigation or plaintiff filings, state clearly: "As a commercial representative, I cannot comment on legal or corporate proceedings. I can connect you directly with Veridian’s corporate communications department."

5. Next Steps

Inventory count sheets will be distributed by Operations by 5:00 PM EST today. Regional managers will hold alignment calls this afternoon. Please direct immediate process questions to Jenna Whitfield or Marcus Lee.

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. is providing notice of a voluntary labeling update for the ApexHip Total Hip System, cleared under 510(k) K162447 on March 9, 2017.

Following Veridian’s September 14, 2021 Registry Signal Review, the Company elected to clarify the Instructions for Use and surgeon-facing labeling regarding patient follow-up and monitoring where postoperative cup inclination angles are high. This action follows review of post-market registry information, including the March 2021 annual report of the United Kingdom National Joint Registry (NJR), which reported a five-year revision rate of 7.1% for ApexHip compared with a 3.2% class average.

The revised labeling will include the following clarification:

1. Surgeons should consider postoperative radiographic assessment of acetabular component position, including inclination angle, as part of routine clinical follow-up.

2. For patients with high cup inclination angles, physicians should consider closer clinical follow-up and evaluation for symptoms potentially associated with elevated metal ion exposure or adverse local tissue reaction.

3. Where clinically indicated, evaluation may include serum cobalt and chromium testing, cross-sectional imaging, and/or referral for additional assessment consistent with the treating physician’s clinical judgment.

The update does not alter the device’s indications for use, contraindications, materials, manufacturing process, sterilization method, intended use, or design specifications. No physical change has been made to the ApexHip Total Hip System. The revision is intended to provide additional clarification to surgeons based on post-market information and does not represent a design change.

Veridian has assessed the labeling revision under 21 CFR 807.81(a)(3) and FDA’s guidance regarding when to submit a new 510(k) for a change to an existing device. Veridian concludes that a new premarket notification is not required because the change is limited to labeling clarification and does not affect safety or effectiveness in a manner that could significantly affect the device’s safety or effectiveness, nor does it constitute a major change or modification in intended use.

We intend to distribute the revised Instructions for Use and an accompanying Dear Doctor communication to ApexHip customers during October 2021. The revised labeling and supporting assessment have been retained in the ApexHip design history file.

Re: Marketing claim history summary for MDL response

Elena:

Per our discussion, below is the requested high-level chronology of ApexHip marketing claims and the supporting review materials. This is intended to assist W&B in preparing the company’s response concerning historical promotional messaging.

1. Launch materials (2017–2018). At U.S. launch in April 2017, the principal positioning was directed to active adults ages 45–65 and emphasized large-head stability, low wear, and intended longevity. The original “Active Life” materials used variations of “built for an active life” and “designed for lasting movement.” Claim substantiation files maintained by Marketing Communications include the 510(k) clearance materials, ISO wear-testing summaries, and clinical literature then cited by the team.

2. “Lifetime of movement” language (2019–2021). The phrase “designed to last a lifetime of movement” first appears in the Kessler Reid brochure draft circulated in August 2019 and was carried into the 2020 Active Life campaign, certain booth graphics, and digital copy. Anika Shah’s claim substantiation review reflects that Regulatory requested qualification of the statement as an aspirational durability claim rather than a guarantee. The final consumer-facing materials included qualifying language, although use was not perfectly uniform across field collateral.

3. Revision-rate comparisons (2020–2021). Comparative revision-rate language was introduced in sales and surgeon-facing slide materials during 2020. Those materials generally described ApexHip’s early performance and, in some versions, compared revision experience with published class or registry data. The underlying review file includes a March 2020 substantiation memorandum, source citations, and drafts reflecting comments from Regulatory, Clinical, and Marketing. Following the March 2021 NJR report, the comparison language was reviewed again. By fall 2021, materials using favorable comparative revision messaging were retired or revised.

4. Retirement and withdrawal. The “lifetime of movement” tagline was removed from newly produced materials during the 2021 label-update and messaging review. Existing field pieces were subject to retrieval and replacement instructions thereafter. Following the February 2, 2024 voluntary market withdrawal, Marketing discontinued ApexHip promotional activity entirely.

The relevant materials should include the Kessler Reid creative files, Shah’s substantiation review memoranda, version-controlled brochures and web copy, and the 2020–2021 sales decks. Please let me know if you would like us to provide a custodian-by-custodian index rather than the chronological production set we discussed.

Please do not forward outside the W&B team without checking with me.

Rachel Steinberg
General Counsel
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

SUBJECT: Hotline Investigation Summary – Report H-2021-047

1. BACKGROUND & SCOPE
On November 18, 2021, an anonymous report was submitted via the Veridian Ethics Hotline (Ref # H-2021-047) alleging that personnel within the Quality and Complaint Handling department were deliberately suppressing adverse event complaint trending related to the ApexHip system. Specifically, the reporter alleged that metal-on-metal wear and metallosis/ARMD complaint rates were intentionally slow-walked or reclassified in TrackWise to avoid triggering premature internal regulatory escalation and external mandatory reporting.

Human Resources initiated a formal internal inquiry in coordination with the Legal department. Over the past seven weeks, investigative interviews were conducted with seven current employees across Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, and Regulatory Affairs, including Complaint Handling Specialists, Post-Market Analysts, and department leadership. A review of relevant TrackWise escalation workflows, standard operating procedures (SOP-QA-402, SOP-RA-110), and internal correspondence was also performed.

2. INVESTIGATION FINDINGS
Based on the totality of interview statements and contemporaneous records, the investigation concludes that there is no substantiated evidence of intentional or malicious suppression of complaint data or adverse event trending by Quality leadership or individual complaint specialists.

However, the inquiry identified material process vulnerabilities and cross-functional communication breakdowns:
* Documentation Gaps: Escalation discussions between Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling) and Dana Okonkwo’s Regulatory Affairs team frequently occurred via informal verbal touchpoints or ad hoc check-ins rather than structured, formal TrackWise or Agile escalation records. This lack of formal audit-trail documentation gave junior team members the perception that concerns were being dismissed or stalled.
* Procedural Ambiguity: While individual adverse event MDR determinations adhered strictly to 21 CFR 803 decision trees per procedure, thresholds for aggregate "out-of-trend" statistical escalations were inconsistently understood between the primary complaint handlers and post-market surveillance.

3. RECOMMENDATIONS & OUTCOMES
1. Managerial Coaching: HR will implement targeted leadership and communication coaching for Priya Raman. Coaching will focus on transparent downward communication, structured upward handoffs, and reinforcing psychological safety within her reporting chain so team members do not feel compelled to seek anonymous escalation channels.
2. Process Alignment & Training: Quality and Regulatory Affairs must jointly update the interface SOP governing complaint trending escalations. Mandatory retraining will be assigned in Workday Learning for all Quality complaint-handling staff before end of Q1 2022.
3. Legal Coordination: In light of anticipated litigation exposure regarding ApexHip performance and registry data, this investigation summary and associated interview memoranda have been shared with Elena Ruiz at Whitfield & Barr LLP.

This matter is considered closed from an internal HR workplace conduct standpoint, pending execution of the corrective coaching and process actions noted above.

MEMORANDUM

TO: Post-Market Surveillance Committee; Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs; Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
FROM: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
DATE: June 1, 2020
SUBJECT: KneeFlex Total Knee System — Post-Market Surveillance Summary (Q2 2020)

1. Purpose & Scope
This memorandum summarizes the routine post-market clinical follow-up and surveillance data for the KneeFlex Total Knee System for the second quarter of 2020, covering cumulative commercial experience from launch (October 2019) through May 15, 2020.

2. Surveillance Methodology
The surveillance protocols applied in this review utilize the standardized Veridian Post-Market Surveillance Registry Integration Protocol (SOP-PMS-042). This methodology mirrors the active surveillance workflows currently deployed across all Veridian reconstructive joint product lines, including our primary hip portfolios (ClassicHip and ApexHip) and ShoulderPro. Specifically, internal complaint intake from TrackWise is cross-indexed against quarterly dataset releases from the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR) and regional hospital purchasing registries, applying cumulative incidence estimates and survivorship modeling (Kaplan-Meier analysis).

3. Registry & Complaint Findings
To date, commercial distribution of KneeFlex has reached an estimated 4,820 implanted units across the United States.

- Cumulative Revision Rate: KneeFlex currently demonstrates an all-cause cumulative revision rate of 1.8% at roughly 8 months of follow-up. By comparison, the aggregate AJRR class benchmark for contemporary cruciate-retaining and posterior-stabilized total knee arthroplasty systems stands at 3.2% for equivalent timepoints.
- Primary Revision Drivers: Among the limited verified revisions reported in TrackWise (n=14), primary failure modes are distributed as follows:
  * Infection / Septic Loosening: 8 cases (57.1%)
  * Periprosthetic Fracture (traumatic): 4 cases (28.6%)
  * Instability / Sizing Mismatch: 2 cases (14.3%)
- Mechanical & Wear Metrics: There have been zero reports of tibial insert disassociation, premature polyethylene delamination, or abnormal metallic debris generation.

4. Registry Signals
No statistically significant performance or safety outliers have been detected across any age cohort or patient demographic. The funnel plot analysis for KneeFlex across high-volume participating institutions remains well within the 95% and 99.8% control limits. No registry safety alerts, outlier notices, or external trending inquiries have been issued by AJRR or regulatory bodies regarding this system.

5. Summary & Next Steps
KneeFlex continues to perform exceptionally well in early post-market tracking, tracking comfortably below competitive revision baselines. Standard surveillance will continue per the established schedule, with the next formal registry pull scheduled for September 2020 ahead of the Q3 PMS Committee review. No changes to the Risk Management File, Instructions for Use (IFU), or clinical evaluation plans are recommended at this time.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
Internal Communications Briefing — Speaker Notes

Date: February 12, 2024
Prepared by: Anika Shah, Director, Marketing Communications
Subject: Notes for internal comms briefing — messaging retrospective

Slide 1 — Why we are doing this

This is not a product relaunch discussion, and it is not an exercise in assigning blame to an individual or team. We need to be candid about how ApexHip messaging evolved, what we knew when particular materials were approved, and where our process did not keep pace with the information coming in from the field and the registries.

Apex was positioned from launch around active adults, large-head stability, low wear, and longevity. The “Active Life” work gave the product a clear identity, but it also created pressure to keep the story simple and positive after the evidence became more complicated.

Slide 2 — Claims used over time

Key language in brochures, speaker materials, and sales presentations included:

- “Designed for a lifetime of movement.”
- “Large-head stability for active patients.”
- “Low-wear performance engineered for demanding lifestyles.”
- Comparisons suggesting favorable revision performance versus conventional alternatives.
- “Confidence to return to the activities that matter.”

Not every phrase appeared in every piece, and several were appropriately qualified in professional-facing materials. Still, in aggregate, the messaging communicated durability and sustained performance more strongly than the supporting record justified.

Slide 3 — The 2020 revision-comparison slide

The 2020 commercial slide comparing Apex revision experience with class benchmarks was created from data available at that time. It predated the March 2021 NJR annual report, which identified ApexHip’s five-year revision rate at 7.1% compared with a 3.2% class average.

That timing matters. The slide was not built using the March 2021 NJR result. But once that result was available, we should have revisited the slide, its continued circulation, and the broader durability narrative sooner. We did not have an effective trigger requiring Marketing Communications to re-open previously approved claims when registry information materially changed.

Slide 4 — What we should have done differently

We relied too heavily on point-in-time substantiation. Claim review cannot end at approval, particularly for an implanted device with long-term outcomes that develop over years.

Going forward, claims with clinical-performance implications need:

1. A named business owner and clinical owner.
2. A defined review interval.
3. Immediate reassessment following material registry signals, complaint trends, labeling changes, or field safety communications.
4. Clearer documentation of what data support a claim, what data limit it, and when the claim was last reviewed.

Slide 5 — Closing message

The lesson is not that Marketing should interpret clinical data independently. The lesson is that we need a disciplined route for clinical, PMS, Regulatory, and Marketing to revisit messaging together when the evidence changes. We should have asked harder questions earlier, especially about whether our old materials remained appropriate after the NJR signal.

Subject: ApexHip Recall Announcement - V-2200 to V-2299

Rob, Owen, Rachel, Marcus, Carlos,

Please be advised that we have formally initiated a voluntary Class II recall with the FDA regarding ApexHip acetabular cups today, June 14, 2022.

Key details per our regulatory notification:
1. Scope: ApexHip cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured at the Cork facility between November 2021 and February 2022.
2. Distribution: 1,140 total units have been distributed commercially, with our current reconciliation indicating 412 units implanted to date.
3. FDA Reference: Recall number Z-1418-2022 has been assigned.
4. Root Cause: Investigation confirmed KinetiCoat porous coating adhesion failures (flaking upon package opening) caused by plasma-spray parameter drift following a routine vacuum chamber maintenance event in Cork.

Crucially, this recall is isolated strictly to the plasma-spray coating mechanical adhesion failure and is entirely separate from the post-market registry trending regarding metal ion wear and ARMD. However, given existing sensitivities around the Apex line, we anticipate that surgeons, hospital value-analysis committees, and potentially trade media may conflate these two distinct issues.

I have copied Marcus and Carlos so that Sales and Marketing can finalize field messaging immediately. We must ensure commercial reps have precise talking points emphasizing that this action is limited to the defined manufacturing window and coating integrity, rather than tribological performance.

Consignee notification letters and physical retrieval protocols will begin distribution tomorrow morning.

Regards,

Dana

MEMORANDUM

To: Sarah Kim, Mike Ruiz
From: Jenna Whitfield, Regional Sales Manager, Southeast
Date: October 12, 2021
Subject: Talking points: if a surgeon asks about the Dear Doctor letter

Team—

A few of you have already gotten questions after the Dear Doctor letter went out, especially from offices that follow the registry data closely. I want us to be consistent, straightforward, and not get pulled into trying to practice medicine from the field.

If a surgeon asks, the opening should be simple:

> “Veridian issued the letter to make sure surgeons have the updated labeling information and can consider it in their own clinical judgment. ApexHip remains cleared and available for use.”

Do not characterize the letter as “just administrative,” “nothing,” or “a non-issue.” It is a labeling update, and the fact that we are communicating it directly is intentional. We can say that the updated materials include additional information regarding patient selection, follow-up, and factors that may affect implant performance. Please use the approved leave-behind and make sure the office has the current IFU.

If the conversation turns to revision rates or metal ions, acknowledge the question rather than arguing with the surgeon. Something along these lines works:

> “I understand why you are asking. Registry information is one input among several, and Veridian has updated the labeling so surgeons can evaluate the current information alongside their own patient population and experience.”

What we should not say:
- “Those revisions are all from bad technique.”
- “The registry numbers are wrong.”
- “Nobody needs to worry about metal ions.”
- “This will not happen with your patients.”
- Anything that sounds like a guarantee, including “Apex will last longer” or “your revision rate will be lower.”

We also should not promise a clinical outcome, a particular cobalt/chromium level, or that a patient will not require revision. That is not our lane, and it creates a problem for everyone.

For detailed questions about the NJR data, comparative revision rates, patient monitoring, metal-ion testing, or a specific clinical scenario, please route the surgeon to Medical Affairs. Send me the surgeon’s name, institution, and the question asked, and I will coordinate with Carlos and Dr. Adeyemi’s team. If it is time-sensitive, call or text me rather than trying to answer from memory.

Sarah, please be particularly careful with Atlanta accounts. Mike, same for any Nashville follow-up from Dr. Rao’s network. These are sophisticated surgeons; they will know when someone is reading a script. Be candid, stay within the approved message, and listen more than you talk.

Thanks,

Jenna Whitfield
Regional Sales Manager, Southeast

MEMORANDUM

TO: Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Steinberg, General Counsel
FROM: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer
DATE: October 26, 2021
SUBJECT: Preliminary Financial Exposure Note – Registry Signal Decision
CONFIDENTIAL / PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL WORK PRODUCT

Following our discussion last week regarding the September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, I asked Hannah Berg to help model out our potential downstream exposure. As we finalized the path to maintain ApexHip commercial distribution supported by a labeling update and the upcoming Dear Doctor advisory, we need to understand the financial parameters should the registry trends in the UK (NJR) and domestic tracking (AJRR) fail to stabilize over the next 12 to 24 months.

Please note that this analysis is strictly exploratory and does not reflect a formal accounting position or GAAP accrual.

Scenario Modeling (FY 2022–2024 Outlook)

Our projections hinge on two primary variables: continued commercial volume and actual cumulative revision divergence against historical class baselines. At our current run-rate (~14,000 systems annually at ~$9,800 ASP), a continued divergence toward the 7.1% 5-year revision rate flagged by the NJR introduces predictable indemnity and defense tailwinds.

| Scenario | Modeled Revision Uplift | Est. System Volume (3-Yr) | Potential Claims Exposure / Reserve Range |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Low Case | +1.5% to 2.0% over class average | 32,000 units (assumes tapering) | $8.0M – $11.5M |
| Mid Case | +3.0% to 3.5% over class average | 38,000 units (steady adoption) | $14.0M – $18.5M |
| High Case | +4.0%+ over class average | 42,000 units (aggressive growth) | $20.0M – $25.0M |

*Low Case* assumes our surgical technique labeling updates take hold, mitigating edge-loading outliers, with claims limited primarily to concentrated revisions and modest legal defense. *High Case* contemplates persistent ARMD and ion-related complications driving formal litigation across multiple territories, forcing substantial per-case settlements.

Recommendations

At present, ASC 450 (Contingencies) criteria for an accrual are not met; loss is neither probable nor reasonably estimable given the lack of active filed litigation and the uncertain causal link to technique versus manufacturing.

1. Maintain Current Stance: Do not book a formal balance sheet reserve for Q3 or FY21 year-end.
2. Quarterly Registry Monitoring: Finance should receive direct quarterly syntheses from Greg Novak's team to track NJR and AJRR curve inflections against these sensitivity bands.
3. Carrier Dialogue: Let us defer formal notifications to Aegis Specialty until Rachel's team identifies a concrete filed claim exceeding standard warranty resolutions.

Let's take this offline before the next Audit Committee prep.

Priya, Carlos—

Attached is the cleaned-up tracker from Meridian data plus our repeat runs: Apex_wear_55deg_rev2.xlsx.

The 45 degree runs are where the original protocol sits. The 55 degree runs are not subtle. I have kept the individual numbers in the sheet rather than rolling everything into the summary slide, because the spread is relevant.

| Run | Cup inclination | Test head lot | Cup lot | Test date | Wear rate (mm3/million cycles) |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| M-45-01 | 45° | H-3021 | V-2050 | 2019-02-05 | 2.0 |
| M-45-02 | 45° | H-3022 | V-2051 | 2019-02-19 | 2.2 |
| M-45-03 | 45° | H-3023 | V-2052 | 2019-03-05 | 2.1 |
| M-55-01 | 55° | H-3024 | V-2053 | 2019-05-21 | 9.1 |
| M-55-02 | 55° | H-3025 | V-2054 | 2019-06-18 | 10.4 |
| M-55-03 | 55° | H-3026 | V-2055 | 2019-07-23 | 9.9 |

Average at 45°: 2.1 mm3/million cycles
Average at 55°: 9.8 mm3/million cycles

That is roughly 4.7x baseline under the higher-inclination condition. We are also seeing the same edge-loading pattern visually on the 55 degree liners. This does not mean every implanted cup is at 55 degrees, obviously, but it is a realistic orientation and not an exotic failure setup.

I know the question has been whether this belongs in the next product review versus a separate technical discussion. My view is we should not wait for the annual review cycle, but that is not my call.

Tom

Re: ApexHip Total Hip System — 510(k) K162447 — Labeling Supplement Notification

Dear Sir or Madam:

This letter is submitted on behalf of Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. to notify the Office of Compliance of a labeling supplement for the ApexHip Total Hip System, cleared under 510(k) K162447 (predicate: ClassicHip, cleared March 9, 2017).

The basis for this labeling update is post-market surveillance data. The March 2021 UK National Joint Registry (NJR) annual report identified a five-year revision rate for ApexHip of 7.1%, compared to a class average of 3.2% for metal-on-metal total hip systems of similar design intent. Consistent with our post-market surveillance obligations, this signal was reviewed internally at a Registry Signal Review meeting held September 14, 2021, attended by Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, and our Chief Medical Officer, Dr. Leon Adeyemi.

Following that review, and based on Dr. Adeyemi's clinical assessment memorandum, the company concluded that continued marketing of ApexHip, accompanied by enhanced physician communication and post-market surveillance, was clinically appropriate at this time. Dr. Adeyemi's memorandum notes that revision rate trends of this nature warrant close monitoring and physician awareness of appropriate patient selection and cup positioning, but do not, in his clinical judgment, establish a basis for immediate market withdrawal.

In accordance with that determination, Veridian issued a "Dear Doctor" letter to implanting surgeons in October 2021 summarizing the registry findings and reinforcing surgical technique recommendations related to cup inclination angle. The enclosed labeling supplement incorporates corresponding updates to the Instructions for Use, including revised language regarding revision rates observed in registry data and reinforced guidance on component positioning.

We do not believe this labeling change constitutes a significant change requiring a new 510(k) submission, as the intended use, indications, and fundamental technology of the device remain unchanged. We are submitting this notification consistent with our commitment to transparency with the Agency regarding post-market safety signals.

Please contact me with any questions regarding this submission.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
QUALITY ASSURANCE — COMPLAINT HANDLING

MEMORANDUM

Date: April 30, 2021
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
To: Quality File
Subject: Complaint Handling Quarterly Metrics — Q1 2021

1. Purpose

This memo summarizes complaint handling metrics across product lines for Q1 2021 (January 1 – March 31, 2021), per Complaint Handling Procedure QA-SOP-014. Metrics are drawn from TrackWise records closed or opened during the reporting period.

2. Overall Volume

Total complaints received across all product lines in Q1 2021: 341, a modest increase over Q4 2020 (318). KneeFlex complaint volume remained flat quarter over quarter (94 vs. 91) and continues to trend within historical norms; the majority relate to instrumentation handling and are closed within 30 days per procedure. ClassicHip volumes continue to decline consistent with the product's phase-out status. ShoulderPro volumes are negligible and not separately broken out this quarter.

3. ApexHip

ApexHip complaint volume in Q1 2021 was 162, representing the largest share of total complaints (47.5%). Of these, complaints coded to the "pain/metal sensitivity" and "elevated metal ion" categories continued their upward trajectory noted in prior quarters. The rate of metal-ion/pain-related complaints per 1,000 units implanted rose to 1.9, up from 1.6 in Q4 2020 and 1.1 in Q1 2020.

There are currently 52 open investigations under this category, several approaching the 30-day per-procedure investigation window and requiring extension memos per QA-SOP-014 Section 6.2. Of the complaints with associated serum cobalt/chromium lab values on file, approximately 18% report cobalt levels above 7 µg/L, an increase from 12% in the prior quarter. This is noted per procedure as a metric to monitor closely given the correlation surgeons have begun reporting between elevated levels and revision recommendations.

4. Root Cause Context

Investigators handling these files should be aware of the 2019 wear-test re-analysis performed by T. Halvorsen (memo to Raman/Mendes, Feb 2019), which identified elevated wear rates at higher cup inclination angles under revised test conditions. That analysis was not incorporated into a design change at the time; it remains relevant context when evaluating whether individual complaint investigations should reference a systemic contributing factor versus surgical technique alone.

5. Recommendation

Given the continued upward trend in metal-ion/pain complaint rate and the increasing proportion of elevated cobalt results, I recommend this data be formally escalated to the cross-functional Registry Signal Review meeting being planned for later this year, so that registry data (NJR, AJRR) can be considered alongside internal complaint trending in a single forum.

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

Date: March 5, 2024
From: Hannah Berg, Financial Planning & Analysis Manager
To: Reconstructive Segment Distribution List
Subject: Q1 2024 Variance Commentary — Reconstructive Segment

1. Purpose

This memo summarizes Q1 2024 actuals versus the FY2024 budget (approved Nov 2023) for the Reconstructive segment, covering KneeFlex, ClassicHip, and ApexHip product lines. Note that Q1 actuals reflect January and February only for Apex given the timing noted below; March close figures for the rest of the segment are still preliminary pending final Concur T&E allocations, but volume and revenue numbers are locked.

2. KneeFlex

KneeFlex continues to outperform. Units shipped were up 12% year-over-year, driven primarily by continued conversion share gains in the Denver and Dallas territories and a strong response to the revised instrument tray bundling that Sales rolled out in Q4. Revenue growth tracked slightly ahead of unit growth (13.4%) on modest favorable mix toward the larger revision-compatible sizes. ASPs were roughly flat versus budget. We did not see any material pull-forward effect from Q4 promotional pricing, which is encouraging — the growth looks organic rather than borrowed. Marcus's team is forecasting continued double-digit growth through Q2, though I'd treat that with the usual grain of salt until we see April bookings.

3. ClassicHip

ClassicHip wind-down is proceeding essentially on plan. Unit volume declined 22% year-over-year, consistent with the phase-out schedule Product Management laid out last fall. Revenue decline was somewhat steeper than unit decline (-27%) due to unfavorable size mix as remaining inventory skews toward smaller, lower-ASP configurations. No surprises here; this line is winding down as designed and requires no further commentary this quarter.

4. ApexHip

ApexHip revenue was $1.2M in January, already well below the monthly budget run-rate of roughly $7.9M, reflecting the sales slowdown that had been underway since late 2023. Following the voluntary market withdrawal announced February 2, 2024, Apex revenue for February and March was zero. This is the primary driver of the segment-level miss discussed below. The withdrawal was accompanied by an increase to the Apex-related claims reserve, which is reflected in segment operating income but not in the revenue variance itself; Owen's team is handling the reserve mechanics separately and I'd defer to Finance/Legal for specifics on the reserve true-up. From a pure top-line perspective, Apex essentially contributed one month of meaningfully reduced revenue and two months of nothing, versus a budget that assumed continued, if softening, sales through the full quarter.

5. Segment Summary

Combining the three lines, total Reconstructive segment revenue came in 14% below budget for Q1. KneeFlex growth and the planned ClassicHip decline roughly offset each other relative to plan; the entirety of the miss is attributable to the Apex shortfall described above. Absent Apex, the segment would have been within 1–2% of budget.

6. Next Steps

I'll circulate the full variance workbook (Q1_2024_Recon_Variance.xlsx) by end of week. Please flag any line items that look off before we finalize for the March ops review.

Hannah
