VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
MEMORANDUM

To: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Date: June 30, 2020
Subject: ApexHip Complaint Trending Report - H1 2020

This memorandum summarizes ApexHip complaint activity entered in TrackWise from January 1 through June 30, 2020. The review was conducted per the approved complaint trending procedure and includes complaints received from direct customer contacts, sales representatives, distributors, and surgeon offices. Duplicate reports concerning the same patient event were consolidated where identified.

A total of 68 ApexHip complaints were logged during H1 2020. Of these, 31 complaints relate to elevated cobalt and/or chromium ion values, suspected adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD), unexplained pain with metal-on-metal bearing concerns, or imaging findings that may be consistent with local tissue reaction. This compares with 19 complaints in the corresponding H1 2019 period.

The increase is notable, although several of the 2020 reports concern implants placed in 2017 and 2018 and therefore reflect a growing population of implants with longer follow-up. The reports are geographically dispersed, with no single account or surgeon responsible for a majority of the entries. Atlanta remains a higher-volume source of reports, but this is not materially different from its overall Apex utilization.

Lot review was completed for complaints where component lot information was available. The implicated cups, stems, and heads span multiple manufacturing periods and component lots. No individual cup lot, stem lot, or head lot represents a meaningful concentration of the metal-ion/ARMD-related complaints. In particular, there is no repeated lot pattern that would support a discrete manufacturing containment action at this time. The current distribution is more consistent with a wear-related or use-condition-related pattern than with a single manufacturing-related event. This conclusion should remain provisional pending receipt of additional implant and surgical-positioning information.

Nine events in the H1 population involve confirmed revision surgery. Explant analysis has been completed or preliminarily reviewed for seven of those cases; the remaining two explants are either with the hospital pathology department or pending return to Veridian. The available analyses describe polished wear areas, linear or arcuate surface scars, and in several cases damage patterns at the cup rim/head interface. Where operative records and radiographs were provided, the cases generally involved higher reported cup inclination angles.

These observations are consistent with the elevated-angle wear concern previously identified in the 2019 engineering re-analysis. As discussed at the time, the standard test configuration did not evaluate all surgical orientations observed in clinical practice. Quality is not making a causal determination based on complaint data alone; however, the alignment between the explant observations and the prior wear-test findings warrants continued close monitoring.

MDR assessments have been completed for all reportable events received through the reporting cutoff. Required submissions have been made within the applicable timelines, and the MDR log is current as of June 30. A small number of files remain open for follow-up medical records and device-return information, but no reportable event is presently overdue for evaluation or filing.

Recommended actions are as follows:

1. Continue monthly ApexHip complaint trending, with a separate review of metal-ion, ARMD, and revision events.
2. Maintain enhanced follow-up requests for radiographs, cup inclination information, metal-ion laboratory values, and explant returns.
3. Provide the updated trend data to Post-Market Surveillance for comparison against available registry data.
4. Reassess whether escalation to a formal cross-functional signal review is appropriate if the current reporting rate continues through Q3.

Legal has been informally briefed regarding the volume increase and the nature of the allegations. No change to the current complaint-handling procedure is proposed at this time.

Priya

MEMORANDUM

Date: June 22, 2015
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer
To: Priya Raman; Carlos Mendes
Subject: ApexHip concept design kickoff notes

Priya, Carlos —

putting down some notes from the concept kickoff last week so we have a starting point before design inputs get locked. this is early, still moving fast, expect changes.

Basic concept: total hip system, Co/Cr femoral head and stem (same alloy family as ClassicHip, proven manufacturing route), paired with an acetabular cup using the new titanium porous coating we picked up in the KBT deal. calling it KinetiCoat internally for now unless marketing wants something else (carlos - your call). the coating is the differentiator here, better bone ingrowth than our current sintered bead surface, that's the whole pitch for going metal-on-metal with this generation.

Target design inputs, draft:

- head diameters: 36mm to 50mm, in 2mm increments. larger heads for stability/ROM, which is a selling point for the "active" patient segment we keep talking about.
- cup sizes: 44mm to 62mm, matching head range plus offset options
- wear rate target: below ClassicHip benchmark (we'll pull the actual number from the ClassicHip DHF, I think Priya has that on file, need the polyethylene wear data as our comparator even though we're going MoM here, different failure mode obviously but leadership wants an apples-to-apples number for the design input doc)
- inclination range for cup placement: still nailing this down, but leaning toward specifying the standard 40-45 degree range surgeons are trained on. more on that below.

Open item — wear test protocol: we haven't picked a standard yet. ISO 14242 is the obvious baseline, that's what everybody uses and what FDA will expect to see referenced. question is whether we test at a single inclination angle or run a matrix across angles to see how sensitive the wear rate is to cup positioning in the OR, since surgeons don't all hit the same angle every time. I lean toward doing at least a sensitivity check but that adds time and cost to the test campaign. want to get Priya's read on this from a quality/DHF standpoint before I bring it to DR-2.

Timeline: aiming to have design inputs finalized and formally approved by September 2015. That gives us runway to hit DR-3 later this year for the wear test protocol decision and start locking down the coating spec with the KBT engineers (their due diligence notes mentioned they don't have a ton of long-term adhesion data yet, so we'll want to build that into our own verification plan rather than just leaning on their historical data).

Carlos — will need your input on head/cup size matrix vs. what sales thinks the market wants, and whether 50mm heads are overkill or a selling point.

Let's grab 30 min next week to align before I write this up formally.

Tom

MEMORANDUM

TO: Owen Park, CFO; Hannah Berg, FP&A Manager; Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs
FROM: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
DATE: December 2, 2022
SUBJECT: Registry Trend Update for Reserve Modeling (ApexHip)

Owen and Hannah,

Per our discussion following the Q3 close and Dana’s request for aligned surveillance figures, this memorandum summarizes updated post-market registry metrics for ApexHip to assist FP&A in calibrating future liability reserve modeling.

1. Current Registry Signal Summary

Data captured through the recent 2022 UK National Joint Registry (NJR) cycle and latest American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR) extracts confirms that the early revision divergence observed in 2021 has not attenuated over time:

* NJR 5-Year Cumulative Revision Rate: ApexHip remains at 7.1% (95% CI: 6.4%–7.9%), compared to the contemporary MoM/cementless class benchmark of 3.2%. The hazard ratio for all-cause revision relative to control hips remains sustained past 48 months post-implantation.
* AJRR Registry Data: US data demonstrates consistent upward trending in primary-to-revision conversions, tracking primarily under diagnostic coding for ARMD, pseudotumor presentation, and unexplained pain with elevated serum cobalt/chromium ion titers.

As a reminder, this represents the continuation of the empirical data set that formed the baseline for our September 14, 2021 Registry Signal Review meeting, during which the committee evaluated withdrawal versus commercial continuation with labeling updates.

2. Correlation with Surgeon Communications and Field Signals

In cross-referencing our post-market complaint tracking against commercial distribution lists, there is a distinct correlation between incoming legal/clinical claim inquiries and clinical sites that received the October 2021 Dear Doctor notification. High-volume implanting centers whose surgeons were directly notified of the high cup inclination angle sensitivity appear to have accelerated patient workups (specifically ordering baseline serum Co/Cr testing and cross-sectional metal-artifact reduction MRIs).

3. Recommendation for Reserve Horizon

Given that the underlying revision trajectory has not flattened, and taking into account the lag between initial radiographic/serological workups and operative revision, I recommend that finance’s forecasting model not assume early stabilization.

Specifically, reserve modeling should anticipate claim volume continuing to rise steadily through FY2023 and into FY2024 before peaking. Assuming revision velocity mirrors historical NJR survival curves for similar large-head MoM bearings, explant rates will persist above market averages across the remaining implanted base.

Please let me know if you require raw data extracts or survival curve stratifications by cup diameter.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
AUDIT COMMITTEE OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
MINUTES OF SPECIAL MEETING

Date: April 16, 2024
Time: 10:00 AM – 11:15 AM EDT
Location: Virtual (via Microsoft Teams)

ATTENDEES:
Committee Members:
- Arthur Vance (Chair, Independent Director)
- Margaret Holloway (Independent Director)

Management & Corporate Officers:
- Owen Park (Chief Financial Officer)
- Rachel Steinberg (General Counsel & Corporate Secretary)

External Audit Engagement Team (Deloitte & Touche LLP):
- Brian K. Sterling (Lead Audit Engagement Partner)

Recorder:
- Owen Park

1. CALL TO ORDER & AGENDA REVIEW
Mr. Vance called the meeting to order at 10:02 AM. Mr. Park noted that the special session was convened specifically to evaluate accounting treatments, accrual adequacy, and disclosure requirements concerning product liability exposure associated with the ApexHip system following the February 2024 market withdrawal and ongoing proceedings in MDL 3102.

2. REVIEW OF APEX RESERVE & MEDIATION SCENARIOS
Mr. Park presented an analysis of the current product liability reserve recorded on the balance sheet ($45.0 million, established and adjusted across FY2022–FY2023). Mr. Park reviewed modeling prepared by FP&A and legal defense counsel regarding upcoming court-ordered mediation tracks scheduled for Q3 2024.

Under evaluated settlement frameworks, initial bellwether resolution and broad inventory settlement structures suggest aggregate exposure significantly exceeding initial estimates. Management presented a recommendation to adjust the disclosed loss contingency range to reflect potential mediation funding scenarios.

3. INSURANCE COVERAGE DISPUTE (AEGIS SPECIALTY)
Ms. Steinberg briefed the Committee on the status of discussions with primary and excess carrier Aegis Specialty Insurance. Aegis previously issued a reservation of rights contesting the applicable aggregate policy limits, arguing that claims constitute separate occurrences subject to individual policy-year sub-limits, whereas Veridian contends the batch clause applies to consolidate aggregate limits.

Ms. Steinberg reported that Veridian has formally retained outside coverage counsel (Coventry & Dean LLP) to evaluate declaratory judgment options against Aegis. Given carrier resistance, management cannot treat disputed insurance proceeds as an asset offset under ASC 450 at this time.

4. 10-Q CONTINGENCY DISCLOSURE DETERMINATION
Following discussion with Mr. Sterling regarding ASC 450 accrual standards:
- The Committee concurred with management’s recommendation to expand the disclosed reasonably possible loss contingency range in the forthcoming Form 10-Q for Q1 2024 to $45 million to $70 million, pending preliminary mediation developments.
- Mr. Sterling confirmed external audit concurrence with this disclosure posture, noting that accrual beyond the low end ($45M) will depend on concrete settlement term sheets emerging from the mediation track.

5. ACTION ITEMS & DIRECTIVES
- Committee directed management to provide formal quarterly reserve sensitivity models and litigation status updates until final resolution of MDL 3102.
- Legal and Finance to submit a confidential memorandum on insurance recovery prospects prior to the July regular meeting.

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 11:12 AM.

Respectfully submitted,

Owen Park
Chief Financial Officer

ENGINEERING MEMORANDUM

Date: March 22, 2021
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer
To: KneeFlex Design History File
Subject: KneeFlex Design Change ECO-2021-044 Summary

ECO-2021-044 proposes a process change to the porous coating application used on the KneeFlex tibial baseplate. This is a manufacturing-yield change. It does not alter the finished device’s intended use, material specification, implant geometry, packaging configuration, sterilization method, or performance requirements.

1. Background and rationale

Since January, Warsaw manufacturing has seen variable yield in the tibial baseplate coating cell, primarily driven by rejects at visual inspection for incomplete coverage at the posterior edge and inconsistent surface appearance in the medial corner. The current process uses a fixed fixture angle and a single-pass application sequence. Review of batch records and line observations indicates that part orientation during the final portion of the pass is contributing to uneven deposition.

ECO-2021-044 changes the fixture orientation by 12 degrees and replaces the current single-pass sequence with two controlled passes. The proposed settings are intended to improve coverage consistency and reduce rework and scrap without changing the released coating specification. The acceptance criteria remain those currently defined in KF-WI-217 and the KneeFlex tibial baseplate drawing package.

This is not a response to a field complaint trend. There is no identified clinical or product-performance issue associated with the current process. The action is being taken to improve manufacturing yield and reduce avoidable inspection rejects.

2. Proposed verification plan

Engineering will build three pilot lots using the revised fixture and application sequence. The pilot lots will be compared against three recent production lots manufactured using the current process. Testing will include:

- Coating thickness measurements at the standard mapped locations, including posterior and medial-edge locations;
- Visual coverage inspection per KF-WI-217;
- Adhesion testing on representative coupons and baseplate samples;
- Surface roughness verification;
- Dimensional inspection of the finished baseplate after coating; and
- Review of process capability for coating thickness and visual-inspection reject rate.

The verification protocol will define sample quantities before execution. Any result outside the currently released acceptance criteria will stop implementation pending Design Assurance review. Manufacturing Engineering will also confirm that the revised fixture can be cleaned and maintained under existing work instructions.

No new clinical evaluation is proposed because the device design and coating requirements are unchanged. Regulatory Affairs will assess the completed verification package and document the basis for determining whether a new submission is required. Current assessment is that this is a manufacturing-process change within the established design envelope.

3. DHF and controlled-document updates

Before release, the following records need to be completed or revised:

- ECO-2021-044 approval record and implementation checklist;
- Updated process FMEA identifying the revised orientation and two-pass sequence;
- Revised manufacturing work instruction and fixture setup sheet;
- Verification protocol and report;
- Training records for coating-cell operators and inspectors;
- Updated process validation summary, if required by the pilot data; and
- DHF index entry linking the ECO, risk assessment, test report, and released work instructions.

The change control package should make clear that yield improvement is the reason for the change and should not characterize current production material as nonconforming unless it failed existing release criteria.

For process consistency, the change-control package follows the same template used for prior ApexHip ECOs; that reference is to document format only and does not reflect any ApexHip technical evaluation or shared design issue.

I will circulate the draft verification protocol by Friday. Manufacturing needs to reserve the coating cell for the pilot run before the April preventive-maintenance window.

Tom

Date: November 2, 2021
Prepared by: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
Subject: Rep Training Deck: Fall 2021 Refresh

Deck file: Fall_2021_Reconstructive_Refresh_vFinal.pptx
Audience: U.S. Reconstructive Sales Organization
Delivery: Regional virtual sessions, November 8–19

Purpose of the refresh is to keep the field aligned on the portfolio story heading into year-end contracting, particularly where competitors are using isolated registry statistics or broad product-category concerns to create uncertainty. Please use the approved slides and speaker notes as written. Questions outside the materials should be routed to Product Marketing or Regulatory.

Slide 1 — Welcome / Fall Priorities
Open with the portfolio: KneeFlex momentum, continued ShoulderPro account expansion, and disciplined ApexHip customer support. Reminder that local market dynamics differ, but the core Veridian message should not.

Slide 2 — KneeFlex: Confidence Through Motion
KneeFlex remains our primary growth platform in knees. Position around reproducible instrumentation, workflow familiarity, and early surgeon experience. Avoid comparative survivorship statements unless the approved comparison slide is used in full. For accounts asking about the minor complaint trend discussed at summer meetings, state that Quality monitors all product feedback per procedure and that the product remains available.

Slide 3 — KneeFlex Objections
Common objection: “I have heard your tibial tray is difficult to revise.”
Suggested response: “KneeFlex was designed with revision workflow in mind, and we can arrange a technical discussion with one of our experienced users.” Do not speculate on individual cases or provide clinical advice.

Slide 4 — ShoulderPro Pricing and Value
For ShoulderPro, lead with system breadth and instrument efficiency. The approved price corridor remains in the regional pricing guide. Do not trade implants for capital commitments without Finance approval. Where a customer requests a bundled reconstruction proposal, involve the regional manager early.

Slide 5 — ApexHip: Current Positioning
ApexHip continues to offer the stability benefits associated with its large-diameter bearing option for appropriately selected patients. Keep the conversation clinical and surgeon-led. Do not use “lifetime” language, “zero wear,” or any unapproved durability claim. The current labeling is the governing source for indications, contraindications, warnings, and follow-up considerations.

Slide 6 — ApexHip: Questions on Metal Ions and the Label Update
This is the section to use if a surgeon asks about metal ions, revision reports, or the October Dear Doctor communication.

Recommended opening:
“I understand why you are asking. Veridian has updated the ApexHip labeling to provide additional guidance on patient selection and follow-up. We sent the Dear Doctor letter in October so surgeons would have the same information directly and in writing.”

If asked, “Are metal ions a new problem?”
Do not say “no issue,” “rare only,” or “nothing has changed.” Instead:
“Metal ion levels and metal-on-metal bearings are established clinical considerations. The updated labeling describes the factors physicians should consider, including patient selection, component positioning, and appropriate follow-up. I can make sure you have the letter and connect you with our clinical or medical team for questions specific to your practice.”

If a surgeon says, “Should I stop using Apex?”
Suggested response:
“That is a clinical decision for you and your patient. ApexHip remains available, and the labeling has been updated to support informed use. I can walk through the updated language, but I cannot advise you on an individual patient.”

Key point: do not characterize the October letter as a “warning,” “recall,” or “admission.” It is a physician communication accompanying an updated label. Do not minimize it either. Surgeons should not hear a different version from us than they received in the letter.

Slide 7 — Discussing the Updated Label Without Creating Unnecessary Alarm
Use a calm, direct transition:
“You may have seen the updated ApexHip label. The update gives more specificity around the patient population, surgical considerations, and follow-up that are important for this bearing.”

Then pause and let the surgeon respond. Do not fill the silence with unpublished data, personal opinions, or claims about what other surgeons are doing. If pressed on revision-rate figures or registry data, acknowledge the question and escalate to Medical Affairs/Post-Market Surveillance. Reps should not interpret registry tables in the field.

Bring printed copies of the Dear Doctor letter only where approved by your manager. The current electronic copy is in the sales portal under ApexHip > Clinical Resources > October 2021 Label Communication.

Slide 8 — Close / Escalation
For product complaints, obtain the available details and submit through the normal complaint process immediately. For clinical questions, use the Medical Information intake route. For commercial objections, involve your RSM and Product Marketing. Consistency matters more than having an instant answer.

Tuesday, September 14, 2021 | 9:00 AM – 11:05 AM Eastern
Location: The Hub, Conference Room Reserve

Attendees: Dana Okonkwo, Priya Raman, Greg Novak, Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Rob Castellano, Carlos Mendes, Devon Mitchell (minutes)

1. NJR/AJRR Review (Novak)
Greg walked through the March 2021 NJR annual report showing ApexHip's 5-year revision rate at 7.1% against a 3.2% class average for metal-on-metal systems. He noted the confidence interval is wide given cohort size but the direction is consistent and stable across two reporting cycles. Late-2021 AJRR preliminary figures show the same directional signal in the US population, though Greg cautioned the US cohort's inclination-angle distribution is not well characterized and may differ from the UK data.

2. Wear-Test Findings Revisit (Raman presenting for Halvorsen; Adeyemi comment)
Priya summarized Tom Halvorsen's February 2019 re-analysis at 55-degree cup inclination, showing 4-6x wear versus the 45-degree-only protocol used at DR-3 in November 2016. Dr. Adeyemi raised significant clinical concern, stating the edge-loading wear data lines up mechanistically with elevated Co/Cr and ARMD findings, and specifically referenced the August 2018 Atlanta cluster (three patients, Dr. Feld's practice) as an early real-world signal that in his view was not adequately connected to the wear-test data at the time. He stated he did not think the company could treat these as unrelated observations any longer.

3. Options Discussion
Dana walked through three options: (a) continue selling with a labeling update including a Dear Doctor letter and revised IFU inclination guidance; (b) market withdrawal; (c) a design change to cup geometry/coating. Carlos noted a withdrawal would have significant commercial and messaging implications given Apex is ~20%+ of company revenue, and that a design change (per ECO-2019-118, previously deferred) would take 12-18 months minimum. Dr. Adeyemi reiterated that a labeling update alone may not address the underlying wear mechanism but agreed it is a reasonable interim step provided complaint trending is materially improved.

4. Decision
Rob Castellano approved continuing to sell ApexHip, contingent on: (1) a Dear Doctor letter to surgeons addressing inclination angle and monitoring recommendations, to be finalized in October; and (2) enhanced MDR/complaint trending cadence per Priya's procedure, with monthly rather than quarterly review going forward. Rob asked that this decision and its clinical basis be clearly documented.

Action Items:
- Devon Mitchell: draft Dear Doctor letter, target completion early October 2021; coordinate with Dana on any related FDA correspondence.
- Priya Raman: implement monthly complaint trending review, effective immediately; report back to Dana and Rob in 30 days.
- Greg Novak: continue monitoring NJR/AJRR data quarterly and flag any material shift.
- Carlos Mendes: assess sales/marketing messaging implications of labeling update, coordinate with Anika Shah.
- Dr. Adeyemi: available to review draft Dear Doctor letter language for clinical accuracy.

Minutes prepared by Devon Mitchell.

Design History File — Engineering Memorandum

Date: 2 April 2019
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
Subject: Design Change Rationale — ECO-2019-118 (Cup Rim Geometry)
Distribution: DHF file copy; cc Priya Raman, Carlos Mendes

1. Purpose

This memo documents the technical basis for proposed engineering change order ECO-2019-118, which would modify the acetabular cup rim geometry on ApexHip to reduce edge-loading wear observed at higher cup inclination angles. It also records the current disposition of the change.

2. Background

Per DR-3 (Nov 2016), the wear-test protocol adopted for ApexHip design verification used ISO 14242 methodology at a fixed 45° cup inclination angle only. That was consistent with prevailing industry practice for MoM bearings at the time and was reviewed and approved by the design review board. No testing was performed at higher inclination angles during original verification.

In Feb 2019 I re-ran wear testing (Meridian Testing Labs, report attached as Apex_wear_55deg_rev2.xlsx) at 55° inclination to evaluate performance under conditions more representative of real-world cup positioning variability, prompted by field data patterns I'd been informally tracking. Results showed volumetric wear rates 4-6x higher than the 45° baseline, consistent with an edge-loading mechanism at the cup rim under elevated inclination. This is a materially different wear regime than what our original verification testing characterized.

I flagged these results to Priya Raman and Carlos Mendes in Feb 2019 (see my 2/14/19 memo). This ECO is the engineering follow-up.

3. Proposed Change

ECO-2019-118 would modify the cup rim profile (increased rim coverage/reduced chamfer angle) to reduce the incidence and severity of edge loading at inclination angles above the 45° baseline, without materially changing head diameter compatibility or the KinetiCoat ingrowth surface.

4. Alternatives Considered

a. Full redesign of rim geometry per above — addresses root mechanism directly but requires new tooling and re-verification.
b. No hardware change; instead issue supplemental surgical technique guidance to surgeons emphasizing target cup inclination angle (recommend tightening guidance toward 40-45° with instrumentation aids) to reduce the incidence of high-inclination placements in the field.
c. No action — not recommended; field inclination variability is well documented in the literature and cannot be assumed to trend toward the 45° baseline on its own.

5. Cost and Timeline (Option a)

Tooling changes for the modified rim profile are estimated at $2.1M, primarily new injection/machining tooling at Cork plus revalidation. Estimated timeline to implementation is approximately 9 months, including design verification testing at both 45° and 55° inclination, updated FMEA, and a supplemental 510(k) or letter-to-file determination pending regulatory review.

6. Recommendation

I recommend pursuing either (a) the rim redesign or, at minimum, (b) updated surgical technique guidance as an interim mitigation while a redesign is evaluated. Given the magnitude of the wear multiplier at 55°, I don't think no-action is defensible from an engineering standpoint, though I recognize the clinical significance of this lab-scale finding relative to actual field revision rates is still an open question.

7. Disposition

This change has been discussed with Quality and Product Management. Per direction from management, ECO-2019-118 is deferred at this time pending additional clinical correlation data (i.e., whether registry/complaint trends support a wear-driven revision signal sufficient to justify the tooling investment and field guidance change). This memo and the underlying test data are retained in the DHF for future reference should the ECO be reopened.

Tom Halvorsen
Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip

To: Carlos Mendes <cmendes@veridianortho.com>; Anika Shah <ashah@veridianortho.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Sep 2018 08:06
Subject: RE: Revised brochure claim: "proven long-term durability"

Carlos, Anika,

I do not support “proven long-term durability.”

Sales growth and favorable anecdotal feedback from surgeons are not clinical proof, and neither substitutes for follow-up data. We have approximately 18 months of post-market experience, not long-term survivorship evidence. The design rationale may be sound, but that is a different claim.

I recommend:

“ApexHip is engineered for durability and stability for active adults.”

If Marketing wants to retain the lifetime-of-movement concept, it should be reviewed separately; I would avoid tying it to durability until we have meaningful registry data and longer clinical follow-up.

Please do not characterize Feld’s or other early users’ impressions as proof in brochure copy. We can revisit stronger language when the registry data mature.

Leon

-----Original Message-----
From: Carlos Mendes <cmendes@veridianortho.com>
To: Anika Shah <ashah@veridianortho.com>
Cc: Dr. Leon Adeyemi <ladeyemi@veridianortho.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Sep 2018 10:18
Subject: Revised brochure claim: "proven long-term durability"

Anika,

For the 2019 ApexHip brochure refresh, I would like to add “proven long-term durability” to the opening spread, ideally alongside the large-head stability message.

We now have two years of strong sales growth and consistently positive feedback from the field, particularly from the active-patient surgeons. Feld’s group and several of the early adopters are telling us patients are doing very well, and the commercial team needs a clearer durability statement to keep the positioning ahead of the legacy metal-on-poly options.

Suggested copy:

“ApexHip is engineered for active adults, with proven long-term durability and stability designed to support a lifetime of movement.”

Leon, can you please review the supportability of “proven long-term durability”? I realize we do not yet have long-term Apex clinical or registry follow-up in the conventional sense, but the statement is intended to reflect the product’s performance to date, design rationale, and surgeon experience rather than a specific survivorship claim.

Anika, please have Kessler Reid work it into the next copy round pending Leon’s feedback. We should keep the language confident without turning the page into a data sheet.

Thanks,

Carlos

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM

Date: January 20, 2021
From: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
To: File / Distribution — Sales Leadership, Marketing, Customer Operations
Subject: ClassicHip Discontinuation Announcement Plan

Purpose

This memo outlines the communication plan for the formal discontinuation of ClassicHip, effective per the phase-out schedule approved by the Reconstructive leadership team. The goal is a clean, professional off-ramp that protects customer relationships and positions ApexHip as the natural upgrade path for surgeons and facilities currently on ClassicHip.

Key Dates

- Final order acceptance: June 30, 2021. All ClassicHip purchase orders must be received by this date; no exceptions without VP Sales sign-off.
- Last shipments: December 2021. Remaining finished-goods inventory in Warsaw will be allocated against outstanding orders and shipped out by year-end.
- Internal systems (Salesforce product catalog, price lists) to reflect ClassicHip as "legacy — discontinuing" starting February 1, 2021, and "discontinued" after July 1.

Distributor and GPO Communication

Customer Operations, working with Legal, will issue formal discontinuation notification letters to all active ClassicHip distributors by February 15, 2021. These letters will confirm the final order date, expected last-ship window, and point of contact for transition questions. In parallel, we need to begin GPO contract amendment discussions — VantageOne and our other national accounts will need updated addenda removing ClassicHip SKUs and, where applicable, adding ApexHip at existing or renegotiated pricing tiers. I'd like Owen's team looped in early given the revenue-neutral intent of these amendments.

Surgeon Transition Support

For active ClassicHip surgeons, Jenna's and the other regional teams should proactively schedule one-on-one transition conversations rather than waiting for surgeons to notice the SKU disappearing from ordering portals. We should offer:

- Case observation/proctoring support for surgeons moving to ApexHip who haven't used it before
- Instrument tray familiarization sessions
- A short leave-behind comparing ClassicHip and ApexHip sizing ranges so OR staff aren't caught off guard mid-case

For surgeons who prefer to move to a competitor system rather than adopt ApexHip, reps should handle that gracefully — no pressure tactics, and no disparagement of competitor products. The objective is a good exit, not a forced conversion.

Positioning ApexHip as the Recommended Alternative

Where surgeons are undecided, the sales team should lead with ApexHip's practical upgrade story: the broader head diameter range (36–50mm versus ClassicHip's more limited offering) gives surgeons more intraoperative flexibility for stability and range of motion, and the KinetiCoat porous titanium coating offers a modern bone ingrowth surface compared to ClassicHip's older fixation approach. This is a pure product-transition talking point — think of it as "here's what's newer and more capable," not a commentary on ClassicHip's performance. Marketing will prepare a one-page comparison sheet along these lines for rep use by mid-February.

Next Steps

Anika's team will draft the distributor letter language and comparison sheet this week. I'll circulate a review draft to Sales, Legal, and Customer Operations by January 29 for comment before the February 15 mailing deadline.

Carlos

Marcus,

Pulled together a quick set of bullets for reps on bundling KneeFlex and ApexHip at accounts where we're negotiating both categories. Positioning is purely commercial — nothing clinical, just contract structure:

- Avoid discounting Apex alone; always tie it to the bundle so we're not eroding margin on one line without a corresponding commitment elsewhere.
- Flag any account asking for carve-outs to Sales Ops before agreeing — don't want inconsistent terms across regions.

Can circulate as a one-pager to the team if you're good with the framing. Let me know if you want tighter numbers on the discount tiers before it goes out.

Carlos

URGENT: MEDICAL DEVICE RECALL NOTICE
ApexHip™ Acetabular Cup (Lots V-2200 through V-2299)
FDA Recall Number: Z-1418-2022

June 22, 2022

Attn: Materials Management & Surgical Services
Northgate Health System
(Affiliation: VantageOne GPO)
1200 Northgate Parkway
Minneapolis, MN 55407

Dear Director of Materials Management:

This letter is to notify Northgate Health System of a voluntary Class II medical device recall initiated by Veridian Orthopedics on June 14, 2022, regarding specific lots of the ApexHip Acetabular Cup.

1. Affected Product Details
- Product Name: ApexHip Acetabular Cup
- Model / Catalog Prefix: V-2
- Affected Lots: V-2200 through V-2299 inclusive
- Manufacturing Dates: November 2021 through February 2022
- Manufacturing Facility: Veridian Orthopedics, Cork, Ireland
- Distribution Scope: A total of 1,140 units across these lots were distributed nationally.

2. Reason for Recall
Veridian Orthopedics has identified an adhesion defect in the KinetiCoat porous titanium coating on the exterior surface of the cups in the referenced lots. In two reported instances during incoming inspection at customer facilities, localized flaking of the titanium coating was observed upon unwrapping the sterile packaging. Internal root-cause analysis determined that this defect resulted from transient plasma-spray parameter drift during coating application following scheduled vacuum chamber maintenance at our Cork manufacturing facility.

3. Required Customer Actions
Please immediately implement the following steps per standard hospital recall procedures:
1. Examine your inventory across all surgical suites, central sterile supply, and satellite storage locations to locate any ApexHip acetabular cups from lots V-2200 through V-2299.
2. Immediately quarantine and cease distribution or surgical use of all identified units.
3. Complete the enclosed Customer Recall Response & Reconciliation Form, indicating the number of unused units identified in your inventory, and email the completed form to Veridian Regulatory Affairs at regulatory@veridianortho.com within ten (10) business days of receipt.
4. Your Veridian Orthopedics sales representative will coordinate return shipping authorization and replacement product orders for all quarantined units.

If your facility has distributed any affected units to affiliated surgical centers within Northgate Health System, please ensure this notice is forwarded immediately.

We sincerely regret the inconvenience this action may cause your clinical staff and surgical operations. If you have questions regarding product return logistics or this regulatory notification, please contact Veridian Regulatory Affairs directly at (574) 555-0144.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.
dokonkwo@veridianortho.com

Rob, Rachel, Hannah,

Hannah and I have outlined three primary paths for consideration:

1. Immediate voluntary market withdrawal (effective early Feb 2024): Results in an estimated top-line hit of ~$70M against our FY2024 projected revenue, plus ~$8M in scrap/inventory write-downs and distributor termination credits.
2. Phased withdrawal (two-quarter runout): Softens the immediate revenue drop to ~$42M in FY2024 by clearing existing hospital commitments, but extends our supply chain exposure.
3. Continued commercial distribution with further enhanced labeling: Preserves projected baseline revenue, though ongoing customer attrition is modeling at -35% YoY regardless.

Please note that our current balance sheet reflects the $18M reserve booked in Q3 2022. With the formal consolidation of MDL 3102 in the Northern District of Indiana last month and initial census tracking higher than anticipated, that figure will almost certainly need a material upward revision at the Q1 close.

Rachel—could you review our litigation exposure assumptions on slide 6 before Hannah finalizes the deck on Friday? Let's take any sensitive numbers offline tomorrow morning.

From: Priya Raman <praman@veridianortho.com>
To: Tom Halvorsen <thalvorsen@veridianortho.com>; Carlos Mendes <cmendes@veridianortho.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Feb 2019 09:06
Subject: RE: 55-degree wear retest results - concerning

Tom—

I agree the result warrants a closer look, but I would be cautious about characterizing it as representative of field performance before we understand the test condition better.

The wear-test protocol approved at DR-3 specified 45° inclination, consistent with then-current practice and the protocol rationale in the DHF. Can you clarify whether 55° reflects a realistic surgical positioning distribution, versus a worst-case/outlier condition selected to challenge the construct? That distinction matters if we are considering any connection to complaints.

Please also loop Meridian Testing Labs in for an independent read of the setup, calculations, and interpretation before we escalate further. I do not want us to overreact to one retest without confirming reproducibility and clinical relevance.

I will review TW-2019-0417, including whether we have implant-position information in the Atlanta records. At present the complaint file has elevated metal ions and revision-related clinical notes, but I do not recall radiographic inclination being consistently captured. Per procedure, we can request any missing information from the reporting sites.

Carlos, please hold any external messaging until we have that additional context.

Priya

-----Original Message-----
From: Tom Halvorsen <thalvorsen@veridianortho.com>
To: Priya Raman <praman@veridianortho.com>; Carlos Mendes <cmendes@veridianortho.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Feb 2019 07:18
Subject: 55-degree wear retest results - concerning

Priya, Carlos—

I re-ran the ISO 14242 wear simulation at 55° cup inclination rather than the 45° orientation used in the DR-3 protocol. Results are attached: Apex_wear_55deg_rev2.xlsx.

Short version: this is not a marginal difference.

At 55°, the wear rate is 4–6x higher than the 45° baseline depending on head/cup combination. The damage is concentrated at the cup rim, with visible edge-loading/scoring rather than the more uniform pattern we saw under the original setup. Co/Cr debris generation tracks with that increase.

I know 55° is not the nominal surgical target, but it is not an exotic placement angle either. We have always known inclination varies in the field. Testing only at 45° gave us a clean result, but it does not appear to represent this condition.

Priya: I think we need to look at the Atlanta metal-ion cluster in TrackWise against cup position if we have radiographs or surgeon notes. This result could explain at least part of what is being reported there. I am not saying every elevated-ion complaint is this mechanism, but the correlation is concerning enough that we should not treat it as routine complaint noise.

Carlos: please do not turn this into a messaging exercise yet. First we need a design review. I want to discuss whether the cup geometry/rim needs to change, and whether there are interim limitations we should be considering.

Can we convene DR-4 this week? This is urgent, not a normal protocol follow-up.

Tom

Attachment: Apex_wear_55deg_rev2.xlsx

Subject: Performance Improvement Plan - Accounts Receivable Specialist

This memorandum confirms the Performance Improvement Plan (“PIP”) discussed with you on September 14, 2018, with Hannah Berg, FP&A Manager, and Human Resources present. The purpose of this plan is to establish clear expectations and provide you an opportunity to demonstrate sustained improvement in the areas identified below.

During the second and third quarters of 2018, Finance management identified repeated concerns regarding the accuracy and timeliness of assigned accounts receivable work. These concerns have been raised with you in regular one-on-one meetings and include:

1. Invoicing accuracy. Between April and August, seven customer invoices required correction after release due to incorrect purchase order references, pricing fields, or billing addresses. In three instances, corrected invoices were issued after the customer had already contacted Finance regarding the discrepancy.

2. Processing deadlines. Month-end invoice batches assigned to you were not completed by the established close deadlines in May, July, and August. The July batch was completed two business days late, requiring other team members to assist with account follow-up.

3. Follow-up and documentation. Notes supporting unapplied cash and customer account adjustments were incomplete or entered after the applicable transaction had been reviewed by the collections team. This has created avoidable reconciliation work and delays in responding to customer questions.

Effective immediately, you are expected to meet the following performance requirements for a period of sixty (60) calendar days, ending November 13, 2018:

- Complete assigned invoices by the published weekly and month-end deadlines, absent prior approval from Hannah Berg.
- Maintain an invoice error rate of no more than one correctable data-entry error per month.
- Verify purchase order number, bill-to information, pricing, and applicable sales tax treatment before releasing each invoice.
- Enter complete account notes in the Finance system on the same business day for unapplied cash items, adjustments, and customer follow-up.
- Escalate any unclear documentation or pricing discrepancy to Hannah before processing rather than holding the item without notice.

You will meet with Hannah Berg every other week during the plan period to review workload, completed invoices, aging items, and any errors requiring correction. The anticipated check-in dates are September 28, October 12, October 26, and November 9. You are responsible for bringing a current status list of open items to each meeting.

Hannah will provide reasonable coaching, clarification of priorities, and access to the existing invoicing checklist. You should raise questions promptly if you are unsure how an item should be handled.

Progress under this plan will be evaluated based on accuracy, timely completion, documentation quality, and demonstrated ability to independently manage assigned work. Failure to show immediate and sustained improvement, or failure to meet the expectations described above, may result in further corrective action, up to and including termination of employment.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
ANNUAL PERFORMANCE REVIEW — FY2022

Employee: Greg Novak
Title: Director, Post-Market Surveillance
Department: Quality / Regulatory Affairs
Manager: Dana Okonkwo
Reviewer/HR Partner: Lisa Tran
Review Period: January 1, 2022 – December 31, 2022
Date Prepared: February 10, 2023

Overall Rating: Exceeds Expectations

1. Summary of Performance

Greg had a strong year. His core responsibility — monitoring registry data (NJR, AJRR) and internal complaint trends for early signal detection — continued to be a high point of his performance, building on the analytical groundwork he laid in 2021. Dana and I both heard consistent feedback from Quality and Regulatory leadership that Greg's registry work is thorough, well-documented, and delivered on time even when the underlying data sets are messy or delayed from the registry administrators. His March 2021 NJR analysis (flagging the ApexHip 5-year revision rate) and the follow-on AJRR review later that year were cited by more than one manager this cycle as foundational to the company's understanding of the signal, and Greg's slide decks and memos from that period are still referenced in current discussions.

It's worth noting for the file that Greg's role in the September 2021 Registry Signal Review was limited to analysis and presentation of the data; the resulting business decision (to continue commercialization with a labeling update) was made by senior leadership and is outside the scope of Greg's individual performance. Greg has, appropriately, kept his focus on data integrity and surfacing signals rather than advocacy for a particular outcome, which several colleagues specifically praised as a mark of professionalism.

2. Strengths

- Deep registry expertise (NJR, AJRR); go-to person for surveillance methodology questions across Quality and RA.
- Clear, well-organized written analysis; decks are described as "board-ready" by more than one stakeholder.
- Reliable under deadline pressure, including around FDA inspection response support in mid-2022.
- Collaborative with Priya Raman's complaint-handling team on cross-referencing registry signals against TrackWise trends.

3. Areas for Development

- Greg has acknowledged that a meaningful portion of his AJRR data handling is still manual (spreadsheet-based pulls and reconciliation), which creates bottlenecks and some risk of transcription error as data volumes grow.
- Could delegate more routine trending work to build bench strength on his small team.

4. 2023 Goals

- Lead an initiative to automate AJRR data ingestion and reconciliation, reducing manual spreadsheet work and turnaround time for quarterly trend reports.
- Formalize a documented registry-monitoring SOP with defined escalation thresholds.
- Cross-train one additional team member on NJR/AJRR methodology.
- Continue supporting Regulatory and Quality on post-market surveillance deliverables as needed.

5. Compensation/Advancement Note

Given the "Exceeds Expectations" rating, Greg is recommended for a merit increase per the FY2023 compensation bands; details to be finalized separately with Dana and Compensation.

From: Tom Halvorsen <thalvorsen@veridianortho.com>
To: Priya Raman <praman@veridianortho.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Oct 2018 16:42:11 -0400
Subject: RE: Explant samples from Dr. Feld - engineering review requested

Priya,

Signed the parts out from the cage on Thursday. I did a quick macroscopic visual check under the bench loupe this morning before sending them over to histology/metrology for dimensional scans and white-light interferometry.

Initial look: on two of the three 48mm heads (TW-2018-0882 and 0885), there's distinct circumferential micro-grooving and peripheral rim scratching consistent with stripe wear from edge loading. Doesn't look like classic third-body particulate from the coating, though metrology will confirm.

Honestly, this is concerning. As you know, DR-3 and the DHF wear simulator protocols only validated these geometries under standard ISO 14242 conditions at a nominal 45° inclination angle. In the real world, surgeons don't always hit 45°, and steep cup abduction appears to blow the fluid film right out. I want to pull these wear-scar measurements and compare them against the planned 2019 re-test protocol we've been drafting with Meridian once we get full profilometry back.

Will update the TrackWise files once the lab runs the full trace.

Tom

Internal Memorandum

Date: February 11, 2019
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
To: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
Subject: ApexHip wear re-test results at 55 degree inclination

Priya, Carlos —

Wanted to get this in front of you before I go any further with it, because I don't love what I'm seeing.

Back at DR-3 in 2016 we locked the wear-test protocol at 45 degrees inclination only, per ISO 14242, and that's what's been in the DHF ever since. I've been sitting on a hunch since last fall that we should be checking off-nominal cup positioning too, since that's closer to what actually happens in a lot of real hips depending on surgical technique. So I had Meridian Labs re-run the protocol at 55 degrees cup inclination on a fresh set of cup/head pairs, same lot family as production, same head material (Co/Cr on Co/Cr).

Results are in — Meridian report MTL-19-0142, dated 2/6/19. Raw numbers:

- 45° inclination (standard, matches our cleared data): ~2.1 mm3 per million cycles volumetric wear, consistent with what we submitted in the 510(k).
- 55° inclination: ~9.8–12.4 mm3 per million cycles, depending on the sample. That's 4 to 6x higher than standard angle.

This is not subtle. The wear scar pattern on the cup rim at 55° is exactly the edge-loading signature I flagged in my concept-phase notes back in 2015 when we were still finalizing head/cup clearance tolerances — I'd predicted this could happen at high inclination but we didn't build it into the formal test matrix because ISO 14242 doesn't require it and DR-3 decided standard angle was sufficient for clearance purposes. In hindsight I think that was the wrong call, or at least an incomplete one.

I know this is a MoM system, so wear debris isn't just a mechanical problem — it's a Co/Cr ion generation problem, and higher wear volume at higher inclination is going to mean higher ion release in patients who end up with cups sitting steep, whether that's from surgical variability or from cup design geometry not tolerating it well.

Priya — has TrackWise flagged anything that could line up with this? I'm thinking about the Atlanta cluster from last August, three patients out of Feld's practice. I don't have visibility into implant positioning on those cases but if any of them were high-inclination placements this could be more than coincidence.

I want to be careful here — this is one lab run, small sample, and I haven't done the statistics properly yet (need to look at variance across the sample set before I say anything definitive). But the magnitude is big enough that I think we need to start looking seriously at either a design change to cup geometry (bigger clearance angle tolerance, maybe a modified rim profile) or reconsidering head material/size combinations to reduce edge-loading sensitivity.

Can we get 20 minutes this week to talk through next steps? I'd rather we get ahead of this than have it come up some other way.

Tom

Attachment: Apex_wear_55deg_rev2.xlsx

RE: Courtesy Notification — ApexHip Total Hip System (510(k) K162447)
Labeling Update Regarding Surgical Technique and Cup Positioning

Dear Dr. Anand:

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. ("Veridian") is submitting this courtesy notification to inform the Agency of a voluntary update to the Instructions for Use (IFU) and surgical technique manual for the ApexHip Total Hip System, cleared under 510(k) K162447.

This labeling update incorporates refined clinical guidance emphasizing the critical importance of optimal acetabular cup positioning during implantation. Specifically, the updated labeling provides explicit instructions regarding target cup inclination angles (recommending placement within 40° to 45°) and anteversion parameters to mitigate potential edge-loading phenomena.

The rationale for this update stems from post-market surveillance monitoring, specifically data published in the March 2021 National Joint Registry (NJR) 18th Annual Report. The NJR report identified a cumulative 5-year revision rate of 7.1% for the ApexHip system, compared to a class benchmark of 3.2% for total hip arthroplasty systems within the same registry category. Subsequent internal technical evaluations and clinical reviews conducted by Veridian indicate that suboptimal cup inclination angles exceeding recommended parameters substantially increase contact stress and component wear.

Concurrently with this IFU update, Veridian is issuing an informational Dear Healthcare Provider ("Dear Doctor") communication in October 2021 to all active orthopedic surgeons utilizing the ApexHip system to reinforce these surgical technique parameters.

In accordance with 21 CFR 807.81(a)(3) and FDA guidance, "Deciding When to Submit a 510(k) for a Change to an Existing Device," Veridian has evaluated these modifications through our internal Design Controls and Change Assessment procedures. Because these updates add precautionary instructions and clarify existing surgical technique without altering the device's fundamental scientific technology, intended use, or indications, Veridian has determined that these changes do not significantly affect safety or effectiveness and do not require a new 510(k) submission.

Documentation supporting this internal evaluation has been placed in the Design History File (DHF). Veridian remains committed to proactive collaboration with CDRH. Please contact me directly at (574) 555-0182 or via email at dokonkwo@veridianortho.com should you require any additional information.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

Dana, Greg,

Per the action item out of the September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, I've opened CAPA-2021-044 in TrackWise to formalize enhanced complaint trending for ApexHip, specifically metal-ion and revision-related complaints. Root cause / effectiveness plan is still in draft but I wanted to get the cadence documented while it's fresh.

Per procedure, the new trending cycle will run monthly rather than quarterly going forward — Quality will pull all open and closed ApexHip complaints coded to metal-ion, ARMD, or early revision, and run the trend against the prior 12 months on a rolling basis. Dana, I'll route the full CAPA record to you for RA sign-off once the effectiveness metrics section is filled in — should have a draft by end of next week.

Date: February 5, 2024
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
To: Quality Systems, Regulatory Affairs, Document Control
Subject: ClassicHip DHF archival procedure

Effective immediately, the ClassicHip design history file will be transferred from active Agile access to controlled archival storage following discontinuation of the ClassicHip product line.

This procedure applies to the completed ClassicHip DHF, including design plans, design inputs and outputs, verification and validation records, design reviews, risk-management files, engineering change orders, labeling approvals, manufacturing transfer documentation, and associated DHF index records. Document Control remains responsible for confirming that the archived file is complete, legible, indexed, and retrievable before the active project workspace is closed.

Per Veridian document retention policy QP-DC-014 and applicable Quality System Regulation requirements, ClassicHip DHF records must be retained for a minimum of fifteen (15) years from the date the product line was discontinued, or longer where required by an applicable regulatory, contractual, or legal requirement. No original controlled record may be destroyed, overwritten, or removed from the archive during the retention period without approval from Quality Systems and Regulatory Affairs.

The archival package will consist of:

1. The final Agile DHF export, including revision history and approval metadata.
2. The current DHF index and document-status report.
3. A records transfer checklist signed by Document Control and Quality.
4. Any paper originals identified in the DHF index as controlled originals.
5. A retrieval cross-reference identifying the Agile project number and archive box or electronic folder location.

Electronic records will be retained in the read-only Quality Records repository, under:

Hub Records Center / Product Archives / ClassicHip / DHF Final Archive

Paper originals, where applicable, will be boxed, labeled “ClassicHip DHF — Controlled Archive,” and transferred to the Hub Records Center at 4400 Silver Lake Blvd., Warsaw. Box identifiers must be entered into the Records Center inventory log before transfer.

Requests for archived records should be submitted through Document Control. Retrievals must preserve the archived record’s integrity and chain of custody. Any copy provided for review must be marked uncontrolled unless issued through the applicable document-control process.

Please complete the transfer checklist and provide confirmation of archive completion to Quality Systems by February 23.

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

Apex Revenue Impact Model — Q4 2022 Scenarios
Prepared by: Hannah Berg, FP&A Manager
Date: October 14, 2022
To: Owen Park, CFO
Subject: Apex Revenue Impact Model - Q4 2022 Scenarios

Attached: `Apex_Revenue_Impact_Model_Q4_2022_v5.xlsx`

Owen,

Per our discussion, I refreshed the Apex model using September actuals and the current field forecast. The model is intended to frame revenue exposure through FY24; it does not attempt to estimate claim severity or timing.

Apex FY22 is now expected to close at approximately $71.0M, versus the $96.0M peak in FY20. The decline began before the June cup recall in the underlying order data. The more pronounced step-down follows the September 2021 labeling update and what Sales characterizes as increased surgeon caution after the NJR data circulated. The recall remains a separate, lot-specific assumption in the model, although several field teams report customers are not making that distinction.

Summary output ($M):

| Scenario | FY22E | FY23E | FY24E | FY22–FY24 Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Status quo / current label | 71.0 | 62.4 | 60.1 | (15%) |
| Label-driven decline | 71.0 | 54.7 | 45.9 | (35%) |
| Full market withdrawal | 71.0 | 48.3 | 42.6 | (40%) |

The status quo case assumes current labeling remains in place, no broad commercial action, and modest attrition offset by existing account utilization. It is the closest to the current Sales operating plan, though I would not characterize it as the base case with high confidence.

The label-driven decline case assumes continued loss of new implanters, lower utilization among accounts that have moved Apex to a limited-use position, and increasing price concessions where distributors seek to retain volume. This case reflects the present trajectory in the Southeast and selected Midwest accounts more closely than the operating plan.

The withdrawal case assumes no new commercial placements after an orderly market action, with only limited residual revenue from contracted inventory and replacement requirements. This is necessarily a planning construct, not a recommendation regarding product status.

For reserve adequacy testing, I recommend using the full withdrawal scenario as the conservative revenue sensitivity. It produces the lowest contribution available to absorb claims-related costs and avoids relying on a recovery in surgeon confidence that we are not seeing in the current forecast submissions.

I have kept the $18M Q3 reserve as a separate line item in the workbook and have not assumed any insurance recoveries. We can walk through the account-level assumptions Monday if helpful.

Hannah

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
Quality & Complaint Handling
Q1 2022 Complaint Trending Summary

Prepared by: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Date: April 1, 2022
Distribution: Devon Mitchell; Greg Novak
Product: ApexHip Metal-on-Metal Total Hip System
Reporting Period: January 1–March 31, 2022
Subject: Q1 2022 metal-ion complaint trending summary

Per the complaint-trending procedure, Quality reviewed all ApexHip complaints closed or opened during Q1 2022 with reported elevated cobalt and/or chromium values, suspected ARMD, tissue reaction, or revision associated with metal debris. Duplicate reports concerning the same patient event were consolidated where identifiable.

A total of 19 metal-ion-related ApexHip complaints were recorded during Q1 2022, compared with 12 during Q1 2021. The increase is concentrated in territories where the product has historically had greater utilization and where follow-up laboratory values are being obtained more consistently.

| Region | Q1 2022 Complaints | Revision Outcome Reported |
|---|---:|---:|
| Southeast | 7 | 5 |
| Nashville | 4 | 3 |
| Denver | 3 | 2 |
| Other | 5 | 4 |
| Total | 19 | 14 |

Of the 19 complaints, 14 include confirmation that revision surgery occurred or had been scheduled based on the latest information provided by the treating facility or surgeon. The remaining five reports involve ongoing surveillance, imaging, repeat laboratory testing, or a recommendation for clinical follow-up. Complaint files remain subject to update as additional operative and explant information is received.

Serum cobalt values were available in 16 of the 19 complaint records. The average reported serum cobalt level among those complainants was 41 ppb. This is materially above the generally cited normal range of less than 1 ppb in individuals without a cobalt-containing implant. Chromium values were also elevated in a majority of records, although reporting units and collection timing were not uniform enough to calculate a comparable aggregate without further normalization.

The observed trend continues to track with the pattern Halvorsen’s engineering team identified in prior wear testing, including increased wear under non-standard cup positioning conditions. Quality is continuing to process each event per procedure, including MDR assessment where applicable, and will provide the underlying TrackWise extract to Regulatory and PMS for their respective review.

Subject: RE: Draft MDR Trend Summary for FDA Follow-Up

Priya,

I agree completely with your assessment.

The submission packet must present the two trend categories in separate charts. Specifically:

1. Present the KinetiCoat adhesion failures (Class II recall Z-1418-2022, lots V-2200 through V-2299) as a discrete, closed-population trend tied specifically to the manufacturing parameter drift at Cork.
2. Present the MoM wear, elevated Co/Cr ion, and ARMD/early revision events on an entirely independent chart under our general post-market surveillance trending.

The coating flaking is a finished-device manufacturing defect, whereas the wear/ARMD reports reflect post-market biological responses and cup positioning dynamics. We must ensure the agency evaluates the recall effectiveness data without muddying it with general wear signals.

This letter serves as formal notification that Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. is voluntarily recalling ApexHip acetabular cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured at our Cork, Ireland facility between November 2021 and February 2022. This action has been classified by FDA as a Class II recall under recall number Z-1418-2022.

Subject: NJR 2021 annual report - ApexHip 5-year revision rate

Priya, Dana, Tom,

The UK National Joint Registry (NJR) 2021 annual data tables were released this morning. I pulled our extract and ran the survival curves for the primary total hip cohort.

The headline number is problematic: the ApexHip 5-year cumulative revision rate is currently sitting at 7.1% (95% CI: 6.2% – 8.1%). For comparison, the contemporary class average across uncemented metal-on-poly and ceramic constructs in the registry is tracking at 3.2% at the 5-year mark. Even when adjusting for age stratification and diagnosis (predominantly osteoarthritis in the active 45–65 subset), Apex is more than double the benchmark.

Most concerning is the revision diagnosis breakdown. A significant portion of the early failures in the registry cohort cite aseptic loosening, adverse soft tissue reaction, or pain secondary to metallosis. This directly mirrors the trajectory we have been observing internally in TrackWise with the metal-ion complaint trend dating back to the Atlanta cluster in August 2018 (e.g., TW-2018-0882 et seq.) and the subsequent adverse reaction reports. The registry signal and our internal vigilance data are now pointing to the exact same failure mode.

Given the magnitude of the delta, we cannot treat this as standard PMS monitoring. I strongly recommend escalating this to a formal Registry Signal Review meeting with Leon and Carlos. Depending on how the clinical review lands, we may need to evaluate our continued marketing stance and labeling updates in short order.

Let me know your availability later this week to walk through the Kaplan-Meier plots.

Regards,

Greg Novak
Director, Post-Market Surveillance
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

ANNUAL PERFORMANCE REVIEW

Employee: Greg Novak
Title: Director, Post-Market Surveillance
Review Period: January 1, 2021 – December 31, 2021
Review Date: February 8, 2022
Manager: Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Chief Medical Officer
HR Business Partner: Lisa Tran
Overall Rating: Strong Performer

Performance Summary

Greg delivered a strong year in a role that required both technical rigor and sound judgment under difficult circumstances. He maintained the post-market surveillance reporting calendar, improved the readability of registry analyses for non-clinical stakeholders, and was a dependable partner to Quality, Clinical, and Regulatory Affairs.

Of particular note, Greg’s work on the March 2021 NJR annual report was thorough and appropriately escalated. His analysis identified that ApexHip’s five-year revision rate was reported at 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average. Greg did not overstate what the registry could establish, but he was clear that the signal warranted further review alongside complaint data, available literature, and subsequent AJRR information. His NJR/AJRR analyses were well organized, traceable to source data, and useful in helping leadership understand the difference between a signal, a trend, and a clinical conclusion.

Greg also handled a difficult presentation to senior leadership professionally. The discussion involved challenging questions regarding whether the observed registry performance could be explained by patient mix, surgeon learning curve, implant positioning, or other factors. Greg remained measured, answered within the available data, and identified the limitations rather than trying to resolve them with assumptions. Dr. Adeyemi specifically noted Greg’s preparation and composure during this process.

Key Contributions

• Produced clear NJR and AJRR surveillance summaries and maintained supporting source files.
• Escalated the March NJR finding promptly through the established PMS process.
• Supported cross-functional review of ApexHip revision and complaint information.
• Improved recurring surveillance materials by using consistent rate comparisons and plain-language conclusions.
• Continued to support routine surveillance obligations despite increased volume and scrutiny.

Development Priorities

Greg’s primary development goal for 2022 is cross-functional communication, particularly with Regulatory Affairs. Greg’s analysis is rigorous, but Regulatory sometimes needs earlier notice when a draft conclusion may affect MDR assessment, external correspondence, labeling, or planned communications. The goal is not to dilute the analytical discussion; it is to establish clearer timing, ownership, and documentation of handoffs between PMS, Quality, Clinical, and RA.

Suggested actions include a standing monthly review with Dana Okonkwo’s team, advance circulation of draft registry summaries where feasible, and a documented escalation path for potential new signals. Greg should also continue tailoring presentations for executive audiences while preserving the underlying analytical detail.

Overall Assessment and Recommendation

Greg is a strong performer whose work materially supported informed decision-making during a challenging year. He is viewed as a valued technical leader with important institutional knowledge in registry surveillance and comparative revision-rate analysis. I recommend Greg be considered for retention bonus treatment in the 2022 cycle, subject to the applicable program criteria and leadership approval.

Lisa Tran
HR Business Partner, R&D and Quality

MEMORANDUM

TO: Dana Okonkwo (VP, Regulatory Affairs), Rachel Steinberg (General Counsel), Dr. Leon Adeyemi (Chief Medical Officer), Marcus Lee (VP, Sales)
FROM: Carlos Mendes (Product Manager, ApexHip)
DATE: September 28, 2021
SUBJECT: Draft "Dear Doctor" Letter – ApexHip Acetabular System Labeling Update

Following the decisions reached during our September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, I have prepared the initial draft text for the upcoming customer notification ("Dear Doctor" letter) regarding the ApexHip Total Hip System.

As agreed by the review team and executive leadership, Veridian will maintain active commercial distribution of ApexHip while implementing an immediate Instructions for Use (IFU) labeling update to address emerging registry trends.

Background & Signal Summary
The primary driver for this communication is data presented from the March 2021 National Joint Registry (NJR) 17th Annual Report, which identified a cumulative 5-year revision rate of 7.1% for the ApexHip construct, compared to an average class benchmark of approximately 3.2% across contemporary metal-on-metal (MoM) hip resurfacing and total replacement systems. While internal clinical evaluations indicate that well-positioned constructs continue to demonstrate strong clinical survivorship, registry data and internal engineering assessments correlate early revisions predominantly with adverse local tissue reactions (ALTR/ARMD) linked to elevated cobalt and chromium ion levels.

Proposed Letter Content & Labeling Guidance
The draft notification emphasizes patient safety, precise surgical technique, and targeted post-operative vigilance:

1. Patient Monitoring Recommendations: We advise clinicians to establish heightened routine clinical and radiographic follow-up protocols for all implanted ApexHip patients, with particular attention to individuals receiving larger femoral head diameters (≥44 mm). Routine cross-sectional imaging (MARS-MRI or ultrasound) and periodic blood metal-ion quantification (whole blood cobalt and chromium) should be considered annually or upon any presentation of unexplained pain, clicking, or swelling.
2. Surgical Positioning & Angle Inclination: Revisions strongly correlate with edge-loading phenomena. The revised labeling explicitly instructs surgeons to target an acetabular cup inclination angle within 40° to 45° and anteversion between 15° and 20°. Operating outside these ranges—specifically exceeding 50° of operative abduction—markedly increases the risk of accelerated fluid-film wear and premature component loosening.

Next Steps & Timeline
Our target mail date to all US and EU implanting orthopedic surgeons, chief medical officers, and relevant risk management personnel is mid-October 2021. Reps will receive accompanying talking points once this text is locked.

Please review the attached formal notification layout (`Apex_Dear_Doctor_Draft_v1.docx`) and provide your redlines. We require formal sign-off from Regulatory Affairs, Legal, and Clinical before Dana submits the final package to the agency and we proceed with mass distribution.

Re: Response to Form FDA 483 Observations dated June 25, 2021

Dear Investigator Delgado:

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. submits this response to the three observations listed on Form FDA 483 issued at the close of the June 2021 inspection of our Warsaw, Indiana facility. We take these observations seriously and have initiated corrective actions to strengthen the timeliness, consistency, and documentation of our complaint-handling and Medical Device Reporting processes.

1. Complaint record documentation and review timeliness

The observation identified instances in which complaint records did not contain sufficiently contemporaneous documentation of intake review, follow-up activity, or closure rationale as required under 21 CFR 820.198. Effective July 12, 2021, Quality has implemented an interim daily review of newly entered and aging complaint records by the Complaint Handling Supervisor. A revised complaint-handling work instruction, QP-198-04, is being finalized and will require documented review milestones, escalation of overdue follow-up, and defined closure approval criteria.

All personnel assigned complaint intake, investigation, or closure responsibilities will complete retraining on the revised procedure by August 31, 2021. Training completion will be tracked through the company learning-management system and effectiveness will be assessed through a 30-day sample audit.

2. Complaint trending and escalation

The observation further noted that our existing process did not consistently document timely escalation of potentially reportable complaint trends. Veridian is revising its complaint trending procedure to require monthly cross-functional review of complaint categories, including clinical outcomes and product-performance allegations, with participation from Quality, Regulatory Affairs, and Post-Market Surveillance.

In addition, TrackWise configuration changes are underway to provide automated aging alerts at 15, 30, and 45 days for open complaint records and to identify records pending MDR assessment. The TrackWise aging-alert function is targeted to be live no later than September 30, 2021. Until implementation is complete, Quality will distribute a weekly manual aging report to the responsible managers and Regulatory Affairs.

3. Medical Device Reporting assessment

The inspection identified instances where the basis for MDR reportability decisions was not documented with sufficient specificity under 21 CFR Part 803. Veridian has issued interim guidance requiring Regulatory Affairs review of all complaints alleging revision surgery, elevated metal-ion results, adverse local tissue reaction, infection requiring intervention, or other serious injury potentially associated with an ApexHip device.

We will conduct a retrospective audit of ApexHip complaint files received from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2020 to confirm MDR reportability assessments and supporting documentation. The audit will begin August 2, 2021 and is targeted for completion by October 29, 2021. Any newly identified reportable events will be submitted in accordance with the applicable requirements of 21 CFR 803, including the reporting timeframes prescribed by 21 CFR 803.50.

These corrective actions are intended to address administrative and procedural timeliness gaps. They do not reflect a determination that ApexHip, or any other Veridian product, has a product defect. We will provide status updates and supporting documentation as corrective actions are completed.

Please contact me if additional information would be helpful.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.
