DESIGN REVIEW MINUTES: DR-3
ApexHip Total Hip System — Wear Testing Protocol & Verification Planning
Document Ref: DHF-0042-M03
Date: November 4, 2016
Location: Warsaw Hub, Conference Room B (and via teleconference)

Attendees:
*   Tom Halvorsen, Lead Design Engineer (ApexHip)
*   Priya Raman, Director, Quality Assurance & Complaint Handling
*   Carlos Mendes, Product Manager (ApexHip)
*   Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs

1. Purpose of Review
The primary objective of this DR-3 milestone was to review and formally baseline the design verification testing protocol for the ApexHip acetabular cup and femoral head articulation, specifically the simulator wear testing matrix required for the planned 510(k) premarket notification.

2. Discussion & Protocol Determination
*   Standard Wear Testing (ISO 14242):
    The team reviewed the standard multi-station hip simulator wear-test protocol under ISO 14242-1 (standard loading cycle, standard 45° nominal inclination angle). Meridian Testing Labs submitted an estimate for a 5-million-cycle run across six test stations and two soak controls.

*   Proposed Extended Edge-Loading / Steep Angle Simulation:
    T. Halvorsen raised a technical proposal to expand the simulator test protocol to evaluate cups under adverse placement angles, specifically adding a secondary cohort tested at a 55° inclination angle to model surgical variance and potential rim loading/micro-separation.

    C. Mendes and D. Okonkwo noted that clearing the 510(k) pathway (predicate: ClassicHip) relies on demonstrating substantial equivalence under recognized consensus standards. D. Okonkwo confirmed that FDA CDRH guidance specifies compliance with ISO 14242 at standard 45° alignment. Running additional simulator banks at 55° would add approximately $140,000 in testing expenses, require securing additional test stations at Meridian, and impose an estimated 16-to-20-week delay on data generation.

    C. Mendes emphasized that market launch expectations require submission in early Q1 2017 to meet commercial rollout targets. Running an expanded non-standard protocol was deemed out of scope and cost-prohibitive given the current development schedule. The review committee concluded that testing at the standard 45° inclination angle alone satisfies design inputs and regulatory predicate expectations. The 55° protocol variation was formally rejected for the DR-3 phase gate.

*   Coating Adhesion Testing (KinetiCoat):
    Per T. Halvorsen’s prior design input memo regarding KBT integration, static shear and tensile adhesion testing (ASTM F1147 / ASTM F1978) for the porous titanium KinetiCoat layer was formally incorporated into the Master Verification Test Plan.

3. Action Items

| Item | Description | Assignee | Target Date |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Finalize ApexHip Design Verification Plan (DVP-011) reflecting ISO 14242 wear test at standard 45° inclination. | T. Halvorsen | 2016-11-11 |
| 2 | Execute contract work order and package sample lot components for shipment to Meridian Testing Labs. | T. Halvorsen | 2016-11-18 |
| 3 | Align 510(k) predicate testing summary structure with draft Meridian test output format. | D. Mitchell / D. Okonkwo | 2016-12-02 |
| 4 | Route DHF Phase Gate DR-3 approval sheet via Agile PLM. | P. Raman | 2016-11-14 |

MEMORANDUM

Date: June 20, 2024
From: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer
Subject: End-of-Period Financial Summary - ApexHip Product Line Closure

This memorandum summarizes Finance’s current view of the ApexHip product line through June 30, 2024, including historical contribution, withdrawal-related charges, and the contingent-liability outlook. It is intended as a closing-period reference for the product line; the underlying legal and claims matters remain open.

ApexHip was launched in the United States in April 2017, following 510(k) clearance, and in Europe in September 2017. It achieved rapid adoption in its intended active-adult segment and became a material contributor to Reconstructive revenue. The line reached peak annual sales in 2020, when approximately 14,200 systems generated revenue of approximately $96 million. That represented roughly 22% of consolidated company revenue for that year.

Based on booked sales through withdrawal and remaining recognized revenue, Finance estimates cumulative ApexHip lifetime revenue of approximately $410 million for the 2017 through 2024 period. This estimate includes U.S. and international sales and is subject to routine quarter-end revenue adjustments, returns, credits, and distributor true-ups. The February 2, 2024 voluntary market withdrawal ended new commercial sales activity, although certain post-withdrawal customer credits, field inventory returns, and service-related transactions continue to be processed.

The financial impact of ApexHip has developed in stages. In the third quarter of 2022, the Company recorded an $18 million reserve for Apex-related claims. At that time, the reserve reflected known and reasonably estimable exposure, including then-pending claims activity, anticipated defense costs, and available information regarding product allegations. It did not represent a final estimate of ultimate loss.

As additional claims were filed and the federal proceeding developed, Finance’s internal range increased. During 2023 and the first half of 2024, working estimates generally placed the potential Company-funded exposure in a range of $45 million to $70 million, depending on assumptions concerning case inventory, dismissal rates, indemnity allocation, defense costs, insurance recoveries, and the timing and structure of any global resolution.

MDL 3102 currently includes approximately 520 filed cases and continues to grow. Case count alone is not a measure of ultimate liability; however, the pace of filings, claimant medical profiles, revision status, and the cost of ongoing coordinated litigation have been incorporated into our reserve analyses. Finance will continue to coordinate with Legal, Quality, Regulatory, and our outside advisors as additional case-specific information becomes available.

For planning purposes, management is evaluating a proposed settlement contribution of $80 million from Veridian, combined with a tentative $40 million coverage contribution from Aegis Specialty. These figures remain subject to negotiation, policy analysis, allocation discussions, and agreement on a mediation framework. They should not be understood as a completed settlement, a final coverage determination, or a fixed accounting conclusion. Aegis’s participation remains tentative, and any recovery will depend on finalized terms and applicable policy conditions.

The total financial effect of ApexHip therefore includes more than the product-line reserve. It also encompasses withdrawal costs, customer credits, inventory-related charges, continuing defense expense, and internal support costs. Those elements will continue to be tracked separately where practical so that reserve movements are not conflated with ordinary operational closeout expenses.

Finance will continue quarterly reserve reviews until the mediation framework is finalized and all claims are resolved. Any material change in the expected Veridian contribution, Aegis participation, case inventory, or accounting treatment will be brought forward through the standard quarter-end review process.

Owen Park
Chief Financial Officer

To: Rob Castellano <rcastellano@veridianortho.com>, Owen Park <opark@veridianortho.com>, Rachel Steinberg <rsteinberg@veridianortho.com>, Marcus Lee <mlee@veridianortho.com>, Carlos Mendes <cmendes@veridianortho.com>
Cc: Priya Raman <praman@veridianortho.com>, Bill Kowalski <bkowalski@veridianortho.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jun 2022 14:15:22 -0400
Subject: ApexHip Recall Announcement - V-2200 to V-2299

Rob, Owen, Rachel, Marcus, Carlos,

Please be advised that we have formally initiated a voluntary Class II recall with the FDA regarding ApexHip acetabular cups today, June 14, 2022.

Key details per our regulatory notification:
1. Scope: ApexHip cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured at the Cork facility between November 2021 and February 2022.
2. Distribution: 1,140 total units have been distributed commercially, with our current reconciliation indicating 412 units implanted to date.
3. FDA Reference: Recall number Z-1418-2022 has been assigned.
4. Root Cause: Investigation confirmed KinetiCoat porous coating adhesion failures (flaking upon package opening) caused by plasma-spray parameter drift following a routine vacuum chamber maintenance event in Cork.

Crucially, this recall is isolated strictly to the plasma-spray coating mechanical adhesion failure and is entirely separate from the post-market registry trending regarding metal ion wear and ARMD. However, given existing sensitivities around the Apex line, we anticipate that surgeons, hospital value-analysis committees, and potentially trade media may conflate these two distinct issues.

I have copied Marcus and Carlos so that Sales and Marketing can finalize field messaging immediately. We must ensure commercial reps have precise talking points emphasizing that this action is limited to the defined manufacturing window and coating integrity, rather than tribological performance.

Consignee notification letters and physical retrieval protocols will begin distribution tomorrow morning.

Regards,

Dana

The Board of Directors of Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. met on July 19, 2023, at the Company’s headquarters in Warsaw, Indiana, with certain directors participating by video conference. A quorum was present.

Rob Castellano called the meeting to order at 8:00 a.m. and reviewed the agenda, including second-quarter financial performance, commercial outlook, quality and regulatory matters, and litigation developments.

MEMORANDUM

TO: ApexHip Design History File (DHF-0042)
FROM: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, Reconstructive R&D
DATE: March 22, 2019
SUBJECT: Design Change Evaluation – ECO-2019-118 (Acetabular Cup Sub-Hemispherical Geometry Modification) – DEFERRED STATUS
CC: Priya Raman, Director of Quality; Carlos Mendes, Product Manager; Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs

1. Purpose
This memorandum documents the technical review, simulator wear-testing results, and final disposition rationale for Engineering Change Order ECO-2019-118 regarding the ApexHip Total Hip System. Under 21 CFR 820.30(i), this record captures the engineering evaluation and formal decision to defer the proposed design modification.

2. Background and Proposed Change
ECO-2019-118 was initiated in January 2019 to evaluate potential cup modifications intended to reduce edge-loading phenomena under steep cup placement. The proposed change comprised a 1.2 mm reduction in cup coverage angle and an increased rim blend radius across sizes 44–62 mm to broaden the functional safe zone during micro-separation and steep operative inclination.

3. Simulator Wear-Testing Summary
Initial pre-market clearance wear testing was conducted by Meridian Testing Labs in 2016 per ISO 14242-1 standard parameters (45° inclination angle, 1.0–2.0 mm head offset). Under this standard protocol, the ApexHip system demonstrated low volumetric wear rates compatible with cleared predicate performance:
* Report MT-2016-0882: *ISO 14242-1 ApexHip 45° Wear Simulator 5.0 Mc Cycle Testing* (Meridian Testing Labs, final report dated November 14, 2016). Mean steady-state wear rate: 0.82 mm³/Mc.

In February 2019, R&D contracted supplemental simulator wear testing at an elevated inclination angle of 55° to assess wear kinetics under non-ideal surgical alignment and extreme biomechanical positioning:
* Report MT-2019-0144: *ApexHip Kinematic Wear Characterization at Steep Inclination (55°)* (Meridian Testing Labs, final report dated February 18, 2019).

The 55° protocol demonstrated a pronounced escalation in metallic wear, showing a 4× to 6× increase in volumetric wear rate (mean steady-state wear rate: 4.65 mm³/Mc) compared to the standard 45° setup. Gravimetric analysis and laser surface profilometry confirmed that steep orientation induces localized contact stress spikes along the superior rim, resulting in edge-loading and rim stripe wear.

4. Rationale for Deferral
On March 8, 2019, an engineering and product cross-functional review convened to evaluate ECO-2019-118. The decision was reached to defer implementation based on the following considerations:

1. Limited Clinical Correlation: ISO 14242-1 at 45° remains the recognized consensus standard for total hip replacement testing. Elevated angles (55°) represent severe boundary conditions that exceed typical surgical alignment targets (Lewinnek safe zone: 40° ± 10°). At present, post-market surveillance data (TrackWise) does not show a verified in vivo correlation between the steep bench simulation and active customer complaint trends.
2. Requalification and Re-clearing Burden: Tooling re-qualification across the full shell matrix (sizes 44–62 mm), updated validation runs at Cork, and potential 510(k) supplementary filings would involve significant resource allocation and lead times (estimated 12–16 months), which is not warranted absent a confirmed clinical failure mechanism.
3. Surveillance Strategy: Rather than redesigning the implant geometry based on extreme simulator parameters, the team determined that post-market monitoring is the appropriate risk control. R&D and Quality will actively track domestic and international arthroplasty registry data, specifically monitoring revision signals from the National Joint Registry (NJR) of England and Wales and the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR).

5. Conclusion and Review Cycle
ECO-2019-118 is formally placed in DEFERRED status in Agile PLM. This design change evaluation will be revisited annually during management review or immediately upon identification of a confirmed clinical or registry signal indicating adverse wear performance in the field.

Tom Halvorsen
Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

2022 ANNUAL PERFORMANCE REVIEW — SELF-ASSESSMENT

Employee: Dana Okonkwo
Title: Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Manager: Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer
Review Period: January 1, 2022–December 31, 2022
Date: February 14, 2023

1. Summary of 2022 Objectives and Results

My principal objective for 2022 was to maintain regulatory compliance and timely agency communication while managing several high-priority product matters. I believe the Regulatory Affairs organization met this objective under unusually compressed timelines.

a. ApexHip field action. I provided regulatory oversight for the voluntary Class II recall initiated June 14, 2022, concerning KinetiCoat adhesion failures in ApexHip acetabular cup lots V-2200 through V-2299. This included review and approval of the recall strategy, customer notification materials, FDA submissions, distribution records, and effectiveness-check protocol. The affected population was 1,140 distributed units, of which 412 had been implanted as of the recall initiation.

b. FDA correspondence. I maintained primary executive oversight of correspondence with FDA CDRH and the Office of Compliance, including follow-up commitments arising from the 2021 inspection and Form 483 response. During 2022, the team ensured that required reports and recall-related updates were submitted within applicable timeframes. I also reviewed regulatory assessments relating to complaint trending and Medical Device Reporting obligations under 21 CFR Part 803, with particular attention to documentation supporting reportability determinations.

c. Legal preservation and cross-functional coordination. Following engagement of Whitfield & Barr and implementation of the February 1, 2022 litigation hold, I worked with Legal, Quality, R&D, Post-Market Surveillance, Commercial, and IT to ensure Regulatory Affairs materials were identified and preserved. This required practical coordination across Agile, TrackWise, shared drives, and individual custodian records. My role was limited to regulatory record identification and continued compliance obligations; Legal directed the hold process.

2. Leadership and Team Development

The Regulatory Affairs team continued to operate effectively despite increased volume, external scrutiny, and significant interdepartmental demands. I prioritized clear ownership of FDA commitments, escalation of deadline risks, and written documentation of decision-making. Devon Mitchell assumed increased responsibility for submission tracking and draft correspondence, which has improved continuity and reduced avoidable late-stage review issues.

3. Areas for Improvement

I would like to further formalize the interface between complaint handling, PMS, and Regulatory Affairs. Although the functions worked collaboratively, the volume and complexity of Apex-related matters demonstrated that escalation criteria can be clearer and more consistently documented. In 2023, I intend to implement a more regular cross-functional review cadence and written action log.

4. Compensation Consideration

I respectfully request that Rob consider a discretionary bonus component tied to successful closure of the ApexHip recall. The recall has required sustained senior-level oversight beyond the original annual objectives, including FDA communications, customer-facing regulatory review, and coordination of closure documentation. Any such consideration should be contingent on completion of effectiveness checks and FDA acceptance of recall closure materials.

Dana

MEMORANDUM

TO: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs; Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling; Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Chief Medical Officer
FROM: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
DATE: September 20, 2021
SUBJECT: ApexHip System Instructions for Use (IFU) — Proposed Labeling Revision Rationale & Drafting

Following the consensus reached during the September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, this memorandum outlines the commercial and clinical positioning rationale for the proposed updates to the ApexHip Acetabular Cup Instructions for Use (IFU-0144, Rev. D) and the associated Surgical Technique Guide.

1. Strategic Context & Objective
Recent registry publications (notably the 2021 NJR Annual Report indicating a 7.1% cumulative revision rate at 5 years) require clear risk-mitigation measures from the manufacturer. However, as discussed with senior leadership, our objective is to provide actionable clinical instruction to operating surgeons that accounts for these registry trends while avoiding an overbroad safety communication or market action that could inadvertently undermine commercial confidence in the Apex platform.

By framing wear performance around strict anatomical placement parameters, we can reinforce optimal surgical execution and address the underlying registry signal without triggering broader market alarm.

2. Proposed IFU Revisions (Section 4: Warnings and Precautions)
We propose adding the following language under Section 4.2 (*Implant Positioning and Wear Performance*):

> *"CAUTION: Clinical outcomes and bearing couple wear characteristics are highly sensitive to acetabular component orientation. Internal bench testing demonstrates that cup abduction (inclination) angles exceeding 45 degrees, particularly when combined with excessive anteversion, lead to localized edge-loading and significantly accelerated volumetric wear rates. Surgeons should verify intraoperative cup orientation using radiographic or navigational alignment aids to maintain an inclination target of 40° to 45°."*

Drafting Note: While this text directly incorporates findings from our internal bench testing regarding high-angle biomechanics, the wording intentionally characterizes this as an operative technique optimization rather than an inherent product limitation.

3. Surgical Technique Guide Additions
We will simultaneously issue an addendum to the ApexHip Surgical Technique Guide emphasizing:
- Verification of the "safe zone" (Lewinnek criteria) prior to final cup impaction.
- Specific warnings regarding patient anatomy variations (e.g., pelvic tilt in high-flexion activities) that can artificially elevate the functional inclination angle beyond 45°.

4. Alignment with Planned Communications
This labeling update will serve as the technical foundation for the upcoming "Dear Healthcare Provider" letter scheduled for release in mid-October 2021. By establishing that elevated wear is predominantly driven by component positioning outside the validated envelope, the communication appropriately shifts focus to surgical precision and patient selection.

5. Next Steps and Action Required
Per design change procedures, this revision will be routed under an expedited Change Order in Agile.

Dana — I would appreciate your formal regulatory sign-off on the proposed language above by Friday, September 24, so that Marketing and Regulatory can finalize the October Dear Doctor communication draft and confirm filing requirements under 21 CFR 803 / 820 before distribution.

HUMAN RESOURCES EMPLOYEE RELATIONS INVESTIGATION REPORT & CLOSURE FORM

CASE DETAILS
Case Tracking ID: ER-2022-088
Date Opened: 2021-12-02
Date Closed: 2022-10-11
Investigator: Lisa Tran, HR Business Partner (R&D / Quality)
Subject Employee: Complaint-Handling Specialist II (Quality & Post-Market Operations)
Reporting Manager: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Department: Quality & Regulatory Affairs (Warsaw Hub)

NATURE OF ALLEGATION / INTAKE SUMMARY
Investigation initiated following receipt of an anonymous Ethics Hotline submission in November 2021 alleging deliberate suppression and backlog manipulation of post-market complaint trending reports within Quality, specifically regarding hip revision and wear-related adverse event clusters logged in TrackWise between 2019 and 2021.

INVESTIGATION FINDINGS
Interviews conducted with department personnel, along with an audit of TrackWise workflows and monthly trend log completion stamps (2019–2021), established that complaint trending reports were completed and maintained in the system. However, recurring report generation deadlines experienced documented operational delays ranging from 15 to 45 business days past procedural targets.

HR found no evidence of bad faith, intentional suppression, or directive from management to conceal complaint trends. The primary root cause was an acute staffing shortfall in Post-Market Operations compounded by heightened complaint intake volumes. While the anonymous reporter raised concerns regarding department leadership, the factual record confirms that neither Priya Raman nor VP Regulatory Affairs Dana Okonkwo directed or participated in any intentional suppression of complaint data.

CORRECTIVE ACTION & RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Employee Disposition: Subject specialist did not engage in willful misconduct. HR recommends placement on a 60-day Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) focusing on workflow pacing, prompt escalation of queue backlogs, and adherence to TrackWise milestone schedules, rather than termination.
2. Quality Process Alignment: In light of the June 2021 FDA Form 483 Observation 2 citing complaint trending timeliness, HR strongly recommends Quality initiate an immediate resource allocation and procedural review to prevent further systemic processing bottlenecks.

Case Status: CLOSED
Investigator Signature: Lisa Tran, HRBP
Approval: Employee Relations Review Board

MEMORANDUM

Date: January 29, 2024
From: Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer
To: Dana Okonkwo; Owen Park; Rachel Steinberg; Dr. Leon Adeyemi; Marcus Lee
Subject: Decision Memo — Voluntary Market Withdrawal of ApexHip

This memo confirms the Board's decision, reached in yesterday's session, to voluntarily withdraw ApexHip from the market effective February 2, 2024. I want to lay out the basis for this decision and assign next steps.

Background. The registry signal on ApexHip's revision rate is not new. The March 2021 NJR annual report first flagged a 5-year revision rate of 7.1% against a class average of 3.2%, a gap AJRR data corroborated later that year. We formally evaluated that signal at the September 14, 2021 Registry Signal Review and made the judgment at the time to continue selling with a labeling update and surgeon communication. That was a reasonable decision on the information available then. It is no longer the right decision.

Since that meeting, the picture has not improved. Dr. Adeyemi's updated clinical assessment, which the Board reviewed this month, concludes that the pattern of ARMD-related revisions is consistent with a durable, product-level issue rather than a surgical-technique or cohort artifact. Separately, the formation of MDL 3102 in December has changed the litigation posture materially, and outside counsel's assessment is that continued marketing in the face of the current registry and clinical record increases both patient risk and legal exposure in ways the Board is not willing to accept.

Taking the registry trend, Dr. Adeyemi's assessment, and the litigation and regulatory environment together, I have decided — with the Board's support — to withdraw ApexHip from the market voluntarily, effective February 2, 2024. This is a market withdrawal, not a recall of implanted devices; existing patients should continue to be managed per standard clinical follow-up, and Dr. Adeyemi's office will issue clinical guidance separately.

Actions:

1. Dana — please finalize FDA notification of the withdrawal and coordinate any related regulatory filings. I'd like the notification submitted no later than February 1.

2. Marcus — please prepare sales force communication so the field organization is aligned before the public announcement. I don't want reps caught flat-footed by customers or press.

3. Owen — please update reserve estimates in light of the withdrawal and loop in Rachel on any disclosure implications.

Rachel, please coordinate the public statement and customer notice language with Marcus and Dana.

I recognize this is a significant step for the company and for the people who have worked on this product since 2015. It is the right one. Please treat the timeline above as firm.

Rob

Event Description / Clinical Narrative

Veridian Orthopedics became aware on 02 Sep 2021 of a revision procedure performed on 19 Aug 2021 involving an ApexHip metal-on-metal total hip system. The patient reportedly presented with progressive hip pain, reduced range of motion, and elevated serum metal-ion results obtained before revision. Information provided by Atlanta Joint Institute identified serum cobalt as elevated; chromium also was reported elevated. Exact laboratory values were not available at the time of this initial report.

During revision surgery, the surgeon reported dark metallic staining and metallosis-like debris in the periarticular tissue. A pseudotumor was identified adjacent to the hip joint. The operative information further describes areas of soft-tissue necrosis. The femoral head, femoral stem, and acetabular cup were explanted and replaced with a non-metal-on-metal reconstruction.

The available clinical records characterize the indication for revision as adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD), with elevated cobalt/chromium levels and local tissue findings. Veridian has not independently evaluated the explanted components or reached a conclusion regarding device causation. Operative report, pathology information, laboratory results, implant records, and explant photographs have been requested from the user facility.

Manufacturer Evaluation

Initial complaint review has been initiated under TrackWise record TW-2021-0938. The event was determined reportable as a serious injury under 21 CFR 803.50 because revision surgery was required and tissue necrosis was reported. Investigation remains open pending receipt and evaluation of additional clinical and device information.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
CHANGE CONTROL BOARD — MEETING MINUTES

Meeting: ECO-2019-118 Review (ApexHip Acetabular Cup Rim Geometry)
Date: April 2, 2019
Time: 10:00–11:15 AM
Location: Warsaw HQ, Building 2, Engineering Conference Room
Recorded by: Tom Halvorsen

Attendees: Tom Halvorsen (Sr. Design Engineer), Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling), Carlos Mendes (Product Manager, ApexHip), Devon Mitchell (Sr. Regulatory Specialist), Dana Okonkwo (VP Regulatory Affairs)

1. Background
Halvorsen presented the February 2019 wear-test re-analysis showing 4–6x increased wear rates at 55-degree cup inclination compared to the 45-degree standard used in the original ISO 14242 protocol (DR-3, Nov 2016). ECO-2019-118 was opened to evaluate a proposed rim geometry modification intended to reduce edge-loading wear at higher inclination angles.

2. Discussion
Halvorsen summarized the Meridian Labs data supporting the wear increase and noted the change would require re-tooling of the cup mold and a new round of bench testing, estimated at 4–6 months and roughly $650K in NRE. Mitchell raised the question of whether the change would trigger a new 510(k) versus a letter-to-file determination; Okonkwo stated that a geometry change of this nature would likely require a new submission given potential impact on predicate equivalence, adding regulatory timeline risk.

Raman reported that current TrackWise complaint volume for metal-ion-related issues remained low (single-digit cluster from the 2018 Atlanta group, TW-2018-0912 et seq.) and that no clear registry signal had yet emerged domestically. Mendes noted commercial concerns about disrupting the "Active Life" launch momentum and asked whether the wear data reflected real-world inclination angles or worst-case bench conditions only. Halvorsen acknowledged the bench testing used a fixed 55-degree angle chosen to stress-test edge loading and that clinical inclination distribution data was not yet available.

The group discussed cost, regulatory burden, and the absence of a confirmed clinical signal at this time as factors weighing against an immediate design change.

3. Resolution
The Change Control Board voted to DEFER ECO-2019-118. The board found insufficient clinical signal and complaint trend evidence at this time to justify the cost and regulatory risk of the proposed rim geometry change. The board will revisit the decision upon receipt of additional wear data and updated complaint trending.

Vote: 4 in favor of deferral (Raman, Mendes, Mitchell, Okonkwo), 1 opposed (Halvorsen), recommending continued monitoring.

4. Action Items
- Raman to compile a quarterly complaint trend summary for ApexHip metal-ion/wear-related events, due end of Q2 2019.
- Halvorsen to continue informal wear testing at varied inclination angles outside formal ECO scope, results to be shared at next review.
- Mitchell to note deferral rationale in the DHF change log for ECO-2019-118.
- Next review to be scheduled upon receipt of updated data, no later than Q4 2019.

Minutes approved by consensus of attendees present.

URGENT: IMPORTANT MEDICAL DEVICE INFORMATION
ApexHip Total Hip System (510(k) K162447)

Dear Orthopedic Surgeon:

The purpose of this letter is to provide updated clinical management recommendations regarding the Veridian Orthopedics ApexHip Total Hip System (cleared via 510(k) K162447 in March 2017). Veridian Orthopedics is committed to patient safety and continuous evaluation of post-market clinical performance.

Recent analyses of international and domestic joint replacement registries, including the National Joint Registry (NJR) of the United Kingdom and late 2021 observational subsets from the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR), have identified an elevated cumulative revision rate for the ApexHip system compared to historical polyethylene bearing benchmarks. Specifically, data indicate a 5-year cumulative revision rate trending higher than aggregate registry class averages, with an increased risk profile observed in implant cohorts utilizing larger femoral head diameters (44 mm to 50 mm) and in constructs where the acetabular cup component was positioned at higher inclination angles (exceeding 45 degrees).

In light of these post-market registry trends, Veridian Orthopedics recommends the following enhanced clinical monitoring protocols:

1. Routine Clinical Follow-Up: Schedule regular follow-up examinations for all implanted ApexHip patients at minimum annual intervals, regardless of current symptomatic presentation.
2. Cross-Sectional Imaging and Ion Testing: For patients presenting with persistent pain, unexplained groin discomfort, swelling, or mechanical clicking, perform cross-sectional imaging (such as MARS-MRI or high-resolution ultrasound) to evaluate for adverse local tissue reactions (ALTR/ARMD) and obtain serum cobalt and chromium ion concentration panels.
3. Component Evaluation: When assessing imaging, verify acetabular orientation and cup abduction angles to detect potential edge-loading phenomena.

Surgeons should continue to report any adverse events, unexpected revisions, or suspected tissue necrosis directly to Veridian Quality & Complaint Handling at complaints@veridianortho.com or via our medical safety hotline at 1-800-555-0194, which routes directly into our TrackWise complaint intake and regulatory surveillance system.

Sincerely,

Greg Novak presented updated NJR figures showing ApexHip's revision rate gap versus the class average has persisted and modestly widened since the March 2021 report. 3. Discussion — Defensibility of 2021 Decision
Dana Okonkwo opened discussion on whether the September 2021 decision to continue distribution with the labeling update and Dear Doctor letter remains defensible in light of recent developments. Rachel Steinberg noted that outside counsel (Whitfield & Barr) has received inquiries from plaintiff-side counsel that suggest state-court filings are being prepared, and that the company should anticipate the first suits could be filed as early as Q1 2023. Steinberg advised the group to document the clinical and regulatory rationale contemporaneously rather than reconstruct it later.

4. Clinical Perspective (Adeyemi)
Dr. Adeyemi reiterated his view, consistent with the 2021 review, that individual patient risk-benefit analysis still favors continued availability for most candidates, particularly lower-BMI patients with appropriate cup positioning, but acknowledged the registry gap is now a longer trend rather than a single data point. He stated he is not currently recommending withdrawal on clinical grounds alone but agreed the totality of registry, complaint, and now anticipated litigation signals warrants continued monthly monitoring rather than annual-only review.
